Another Round: Trap. A 4-mana blink-your-own-team sorcery with an X that only scales ETB value, and the 41.8% GIH WR plus -8.9 IWD confirm it does nothing on an empty or unsynergized board. The D grade is right; leave it in the pack unless you're a dedicated GW ETB deck, and even then it's marginal.
Archangel of Tithes: First-pick bomb. A 3/5 flier for 1WWW that taxes both attacks and blocks warps combat every turn it's untapped, and the 55.2% GIH is dragged down by the WWW cost, not the card's power. Slam it and build white; in a go-wide GW shell it's backbreaking.
Armored Armadillo: Filler blocker. A 0/4 ward wall that curbs early aggression and can eventually pump into a threat, but the 50.4% GIH WR and negative IWD confirm it's a low-impact card that does nothing proactive. Play it only as a late defensive body in a slow deck.
Aven Interrupter: Premium first-pick uncommon-power in a rare shell — a 2/2 flash flier that Time Walks a spell (exiling it to plot, so they lose it this turn) while taxing the format's rampant recursion. Flexible tempo-plus-disruption that any white deck runs; the taxing clause is real free upside against Lively Dirge/Back for More.
Bounding Felidar: Solid finisher, edging toward a bomb in a developed GW board. A 4/7 body blocks everything, and the saddled attack anthems your whole team plus a huge lifeswing — LoL calls it 'nearly unbeatable once resolved.' The flat 54.8% GIH WR is dragged down by clunky six-mana openers; in the go-wide S-tier deck it wants, it overperforms. Early pick.
Bovine Intervention: Filler removal at best. Instant-speed destroy hits artifacts or creatures, but handing the opponent a 2/2 Ox is real tempo/board loss, and the sub-50 GIH WR plus C- grade confirm it plays like the worst removal in white. Only run it when you're short on answers, and prefer it against bombs where the token doesn't matter.
Bridled Bighorn: Solid GW playable, not a priority. A 3/4 vigilance for four is a fine body, and while saddled it snowballs tokens, but the negative iwd and middling 54% GIH WR say it's a role-player that only shines in the go-wide S-tier GW Mounts shell — take it mid-pack, don't reach.
Claim Jumper: Solid early playable, not the bomb its rare stamp suggests. A 3/3 vigilance for 3 is a fine curve body; the land-ramp catch-up ability only fires when you're behind and near-zero IWD confirms it's mostly a vanilla beater. First-few-picks filler that makes any white deck.
Dust Animus: Premium early pick and a white staple — a 2-mana 2/3 flier that becomes a 4/5 lifelink flier once you hit five lands, with plot as late-game flexibility. 61.2% GIH with a top ALSA of 1.5 confirms it's a first-pick-quality flexible threat in any white deck.
Eriette's Lullaby: Solid role-player removal, not premium: the tapped restriction means it kills attackers/blockers or things you've tapped down, not a clean answer to a resting bomb. The 53% GIH undersells efficient removal. Best in UW/UB, where it also enables Nimble Brigand's crime-and-draw.
Final Showdown: Premium first-pick-quality removal in white — a one-mana Spree that scales into a full wrath (3WW to Destroy all creatures) plus flexible ability-strip and indestructible protection modes. 60.7% GIH with elite 86% play rate; the board-wipe half is a game-ender in the grindy GW mirror, and the cheaper modes keep it never-dead. Slam it.
Fortune, Loyal Steed: Solid early pick and a premier GW Mount. A 2/4 that scries 2 on ETB blocks well immediately, and once saddled the blink resets ETBs and dodges removal. 57.7% GIH with a 92% play rate is a clean playable that only gets better in a go-wide GW shell.
Frontier Seeker: Solid GW playable. A 2/1 for two that digs five deep for a Mount or Plains is a fine early body with card selection, and 57.7% GIH on an 86% play rate is a real number, not soup inflation. Higher pick in GW Mounts where it reliably hits; a functional filler two-drop elsewhere.
Getaway Glamer: Solid flexible playable, better than its C+ grade and 58.6% GIH suggests. The {1} blink mode is a fog/save-your-guy/reuse-ETB trick and the {2} mode is conditional removal; one white pip means any white deck runs it. Not premium removal, but a clean value instant.
High Noon: Trap rare. The one-spell-per-turn lock hurts you as often as the opponent and the 5-damage mode needs red mana, so it's a niche hate-piece; 47.9% GIH WR with a brutal -3.4 IWD and the C- grade say leave it out of a normal 40.
Holy Cow: Solid white common and a fine playable everywhere — a 2/2 flash flier that gains 2 and scries is unexciting on rate but the 57% GIH WR reflects genuine flexibility. Best in UW 'didn't cast from hand' shells where flashing it in end-of-turn feeds payoffs, but every white deck happily runs it.
Inventive Wingsmith: Filler common that punishes your own tempo. A 2/4 wall is fine defensively, but the flying-counter clause demands you skip casting from hand, which fights how you actually want to play. Negative iwd (-1.6) and a 16.8% play rate confirm it's a fringe body — a UW 'didn't cast' shell only, otherwise a sideboard card.
Lassoed by the Law: Premium white removal and an early pick. Single-pip {3}{W} exiles ANY nonland permanent (bomb, planeswalker, artifact) until it leaves, then leaves a 1/1 that pumps your team — a 61% GIH WR with a 2.5 ALSA and 93% play rate. Splashable, flexible, and answers what other white can't. Take it over most creatures.
Mystical Tether: Premium white removal and one of the best commons for any white deck. 2W exile of any creature or artifact (flash for two more) answers bombs cleanly, and exile matters against this set's rampant recursion. 91.9% play rate, +2.0 iwd, ALSA 3.4 — the numbers underrate it; grab it P1-P3.
Nurturing Pixie: Role-player, not a slam despite the tempting flyer-plus-value line. Negative IWD and a 53% play rate tell the story: rebuying your own ETB is cute but the 1/1 flying body is fragile and you often have nothing worth bouncing. Fine in GW/UW tempo, easily cuttable.
Omenport Vigilante: Solid aggressive two-drop for crime decks (BR/UB) — a 2/2 that swings as a 4/4-worth double striker whenever you've committed a crime, which is trivial with removal or crime-deserts. 54.5% GIH and a flat iwd say it's a fine role-player, not a bomb; take it as an early-game body in crime shells.
One Last Job: Solid value payoff, not a first-pick despite the rare tag. The 54% GIH and high play rate ride the flexible spree modes reanimating your best dead creature or re-attaching an Aura/Equipment. A grindy BW/GW recursion card that needs a stocked graveyard to shine; filler-plus in aggro.
Outlaw Medic: Solid two-drop filler for white decks — a 1/3 lifelink body that replaces itself on death, so it trades up, blocks aggro, and never feels bad. 55.4% GIH is strong for a common speed-bump; good glue in GW/RW go-wide, though it's a role-player, not a priority pick.
Prairie Dog: Solid two-drop, best in UW/plot decks. A 2/2 lifelink that grows if you skip casting from hand rewards the same not-from-hand play as Wrangler, but it's fine anywhere as a late mana sink. 57.0% GIH backs the B- read; take it as a reliable early body.
Prosperity Tycoon: Strong white common-slot uncommon. 4/2 for four that leaves behind a repeatable pump token, and the sac-for-indestructible line makes it grindy value that dodges removal. 57.8% GIH and a B grade agree; a high, dependable pick for any white deck, especially GW/RW go-wide.
Requisition Raid: Role-player/sideboard flex. Base cost plus modes means artifact/enchantment destruction main-decks poorly (negative IWD, 45% play rate), but the +1/+1-counter-anthem mode gives a go-wide GW/RW deck a real payoff. Maindeck only when you have the board to pump; otherwise a board answer.
Rustler Rampage: Marginal combat trick. A one-mana Spree instant that untaps a team or grants double strike is flexible but needs the right board, and the 51.8% GIH WR marks it a fringe playable. Fine filler in a go-wide GW/RW aggro deck, cuttable elsewhere.
Shepherd of the Clouds: High pick and one of the better white uncommons — a 4/3 flyer/vigilance that rebuys any 3-drop-or-less, and with a Mount out it reanimates directly onto the board. 59% GIH WR with strong IWD; the value engine shines in GW recursion but it's a fine standalone body in any white deck.
Sheriff of Safe Passage: Good aggressive playable that scales with your board. Cast on a full board it's a big body; plotting it lets you deploy something else first, then drop it fat and free next turn. B- grade slightly outruns the 52.2% GIH WR — it's a role-player in go-wide GW/RW, not a bomb. Mid-pick.
Stagecoach Security: Solid GW playable and a fine common. A 4/5 body that gives your board +1/+1 and vigilance is a real go-wide combat swing, and the Plot option lets you bank a double-spell turn. The flat +0.4 IWD shows it wins by being on the board early, not drawn late — a midgame curve-topper, not a bomb.
Steer Clear: Cheap conditional combat trick, a filler playable. One mana for 2 damage (4 if you control a Mount) only hits attackers/blockers, so it's a combat-only answer that whiffs on the stack. Fine in aggressive GW/RW Mounts decks; the 42.7% play rate and negative iwd mark it as a late fill, not a removal spell.
Sterling Keykeeper: Solid white common, better than its C grade — a repeatable tapper that locks down a blocker or clears an attacker every turn. 55% GIH is real; the non-Mount clause matters little. Good filler for any white deck, quietly strong in the go-wide GW/RW plans.
Sterling Supplier: Filler flier — a 5-mana 3/4 flying that counters up another creature on ETB. 56.3% GIH looks fine but the 6.4 ALSA and modest play rate mark it as a replaceable late-game body; playable evasion in slower white decks but you cut it when your curve fills out.
Take Up the Shield: Above-average combat trick, one of the better ones: +1/+1 counter makes the buff permanent, and indestructible plus lifelink blows out fights and racing. +1.8 IWD and 57.6% GIH back it. Note it's indestructible, not protection, so it doesn't dodge targeted removal or bounce.
Thunder Lasso: Filler equipment, C- and only 44.8% played for good reason — the tap-on-attack is a pseudo-Falter but you're paying 3 to enter plus 2 to re-equip, all card disadvantage if it's answered. Flat -0.8 IWD confirms it doesn't move games. Late playable in an aggressive GW/RW go-wide deck only.
Trained Arynx: Good aggressive common, the RW/GW go-wide two-drop. A 3/1 that gains first strike when saddled trades up and pushes damage; 57.3% GIH and a 4.3 ALSA make it a strong early creature. The high oh_wr (59.7%) confirms it wants to be on the play attacking.
Vengeful Townsfolk: Role-player. A vanilla 3/3 for three that only grows in a sacrifice/attrition shell, and the 54.3% GIH with -0.9 IWD says the counter rarely matters — you're mostly paying for the body. Fine curve filler in BW/BR grind; nothing you prioritize.
Wanted Griffin: Fine filler flier for white decks. 3/2 flying that leaves a 1/1 Mercenary is a reasonable two-body common, and 54.9% GIH is a serviceable back-half creature, but the low play rate says it's a 22nd-card body, not a card you prioritize. Take it late.
Archmage's Newt: Solid role-player for UR/spells decks. A 2/2 flyer Mount that reflashes an instant/sorcery on hit (free when saddled) is real recursion for a double-spell shell, but the modest 52.4% GIH WR shows it's a builder's card, not a slam. Best in UR late-game control.
Canyon Crab: Wildly underdrafted blue uncommon — a 0/5 wall that loots every turn you don't cast from hand and can swing as a 2/3. The doctrine flags it as a blue-is-open signal: seeing it pick 6-7+ means UW/UR late-game control is wide open. Take it and lean into the plot/flash shell that hosts love.
Daring Thunder-Thief: Serviceable filler for Ux tempo/control. A flash 4/4 for four that enters tapped means you're ambush-blocking then attacking next turn — fine value but no evasion or ETB. The +1.4 iwd shows it plays better than it looks, but a 17.6% play rate marks it as a late playable, not a priority.
Deepmuck Desperado: Role-player mill enabler for UB crime, not a beater. The 2/4 body blocks well, but its once-a-turn mill-3 only matters if you're grinding a Grindstone/self-mill win or just chipping a control opponent's library. The 52.6% WR is soft; play it in UB as a 3-drop wall that does incidental work, C- otherwise.
Djinn of Fool's Fall: Filler flier. A 4/3 flyer for five with plot is playable evasion but nothing more — the 50.2% GIH WR and weak 47.5% OH WR flag it as a curve-topper you play when short on fliers. Plot lets you deploy it while passing with mana open in a UW/UR control shell, but it's a late pick.
Double Down: Build-around mythic that lives and dies on outlaw density — the +6.0 IWD is a UB/BR crime-and-outlaws deck's number, not a random slam. Copying removal or an outlaw ETB snowballs games, but in a deck light on outlaws it's a do-nothing enchantment. High pick only when committed to BR/UB.
Duelist of the Mind: High pick in crime-leaning blue (UB/UW) — a 2-mana */3 flier with vigilance that grows with cards drawn and loots on your first crime each turn, both drawing and turning on other payoffs. +7.5 iwd and 58.4% GIH reflect a genuine engine; prioritize it when you're on crimes.
Emergent Haunting: Sneaky-good uncommon that wheels to pick 6+; a 3/3 flyer for 1U that also sinks late mana into surveil. The +2.1 IWD confirms it overperforms. Best in UW/UR shells that naturally leave mana up and pass (plot synergy) — worse in a hellbent aggro deck. Grab it late; blue is open.
Failed Fording: Serviceable but replaceable tempo bounce — 1U to return any nonland permanent, with a desert-conditional surveil upside. Bounce is card disadvantage, so the 53.6% GIH and low 37.6% play rate read as fringe; fine as a cheap answer to a bomb or Mount in a UB/UW control shell, otherwise a late pick.
Fblthp, Lost on the Range: Trap despite the rare tag. A 1/1 Ward 2 that plots your top card is cute but slow, and 47.6% GIH with negative IWD says it doesn't pull its weight. Only playable in a dedicated plot/UW value build; pass it for real creatures or removal.
Fleeting Reflection: Filler/sideboard. A two-mana hexproof-plus-clone combat trick that's clunky: it needs a good copy target to blow anyone out, and the 8.6% play rate with 48% GIH shows most decks correctly cut it. The 50.4% GD WR hints it can steal games, but it's a niche Ux card, not a maindeck staple.
Geralf, the Fleshwright: Strong build-around bomb for UB/spells decks. +6.7 IWD and 1.7 ALSA say it overperforms and goes early; double-spelling snowballs growing Zombies fast. It's a 2/3 that needs a critical mass of cheap spells to hum, so lean UB crime/tempo — but the number is real, not soup inflation.
Geyser Drake: Fine playable. A 2/3 flyer for three that quietly discounts your instant-speed spells on the opponent's turn — evasive body plus incidental upside. The 51.6% GIH WR and +1.6 IWD peg it as a serviceable blue common, better in a control/flash-heavy UR/UW deck.
Harrier Strix: Marginal filler common — a 1/1 flyer that taps a permanent on ETB (a pseudo-Falter or blocker-tapper) with a clunky {2}{U} loot. 27% play rate and weak OH WR mark it as a late blue role-player; only makes the deck when you need evasion and card selection, and even then it's near the bottom.
Jailbreak Scheme: Sneaky-strong combat trick and the WR proves it — 56.1% GIH with a huge +4.3 iwd. The +1/+1-and-unblockable mode ends games out of nowhere, and the bounce mode is flexible tempo/removal. C grade badly underrates it; the spree flexibility makes it a real playable in any blue deck, especially UB/UW tempo. Take it over most commons.
The Key to the Vault: Trap rare; leave it. It only pays off after connecting for combat damage and demands you build around evasion, then the returns are slow — a 43.7% GIH WR, D grade, and 16% play rate say the format is too fast for a do-nothing equipment. Sideboard filler in a dedicated flyers deck at most.
Loan Shark: Solid blue common and a real curve piece. A 3/4 for four blocks the format's aggressive starts well, and the +3.3 iwd plus B grade reward the body more than the conditional draw. In a UR/UB double-spell shell the draw and plot both come online; take it as a dependable mid-pick regardless.
Marauding Sphinx: Premium blue uncommon and a near-slam for UB control — a 5-mana 3/5 flying vigilance ward 2 is a house on stats alone, and the surveil-on-crime is pure gravy since you're committing crimes anyway. 57.9% GIH with a strong OH; take it early and let blue signals guide you.
Metamorphic Blast: Flexible blue instant that's better as removal than the numbers suggest — the {1} mode shrinks any creature to a 0/1 (killing it in combat or neutering a bomb), and {3} refills. 56.1% GIH with removal underrated by GIH WR; a solid playable that scales, best in UB/UW control.
Nimble Brigand: Good aggressive engine for UB/BR crime — a 1/3 that goes unblockable and draws a card whenever you've committed a crime, which is trivially easy with removal or the crime-deserts. +3.5 IWD shows it snowballs. Don't hold crimes for it; just play it and let natural targeting turn it on.
Outlaw Stitcher: Doctrine-flagged trap uncommon — the 1/4 body is fine but the payoff needs multiple spells in one turn to make a real token, which your deck usually can't reliably set up. 53.8% GIH is unremarkable for a B-graded uncommon; the plot option is the appealing part. Take it as a body, not a build-around.
Peerless Ropemaster: Filler / late roleplayer, mainly UW/UB tempo. A 4/4 for five that only bounces a TAPPED creature is a weak tempo swing, and the 21.9% play rate shows most cut it. 54.9% GIH is deck-dependent padding — playable as a body but never a priority.
Phantom Interference: The doctrine trap. A one-mana Spree that's either a bad Mausoleum Secrets token or a soft counter, and hosts cooled hard on it mid-format ("not it") because holding up mana punishes your own gameplan. The 56.7% GIH is inflated by control pilots; take it low as flexible UW/UB filler, not a priority.
Plan the Heist: Premium card advantage, better than its C grade. LoL: "three-for-ones are the new two-for-ones" — drawing three (surveil 3 if hipster empty) plus a Plot option makes it a control staple in UB/UW. 56.9% GIH with high gd_wr is the mark of a late-game engine, not a tempo play.
Razzle-Dazzler: Trap for most drafters. The 1/2 grows and connects only if you reliably cast two spells a turn, and the doctrine flags Razzle-Dazzler UR aggro as a build-around that fails unless the whole deck is low-curve. The 50.8% GIH WR is a mirage; skip unless fully committed to UR tempo.
Seize the Secrets: Fringe blue common — Divination that costs {1}{U} after a crime. The 53.6% GIH WR is a UB-crimes number (LoL), not a slam; the gap between drawn and opening-hand WR marks it as a synergy card. Playable card advantage when you're crime-dense, otherwise a low-priority slot-filler.
Shackle Slinger: Role-player for a spell-dense Ux deck. A 3/2 for three that repeatedly taps/stuns down an opponent's creature on your second spell each turn — real tempo, but the trigger is conditional and the body dies to everything. The 50.1% GIH masks a +2.9 iwd; playable in UR/UB double-spell shells, filler elsewhere.
Shifting Grift: Niche build-around, essentially unplayable maindeck. Swapping creatures needs a huge board disparity to be worth {U}{U}+{2}, and the 6% play rate with a 7.7 ALSA shows nobody wants it. The C+ grade is theory; the 46% WR is the truth. Skip unless you're a control deck stealing their only bomb.
Slickshot Lockpicker: One of the best uncommons in the set and a signal blue is open — LoL notes it goes embarrassingly late (ALSA 3.8). A 2/3 Snapcaster that re-buys your best instant/sorcery, with plot flexibility. Elite in UB/UW/UR spells shells; the +4.6 iwd and 58.8% drawn WR confirm the ceiling. Prioritize it.
Slickshot Vault-Buster: Filler at best, basically a sideboard card. A 1/4 that swings to 3/4 only when you've committed a crime is a weak clock, and sub-50% GIH with a 15% play rate is damning. The set's worst common tier — leave it in the pool unless you're desperate for a two-drop.
Spring Splasher: Filler at best — a fragile 2/1 that gives a blocker -3/-0 on attack, which only matters if you're the aggressor. 50.2% GIH and a 30.8% play rate (identical OH/GD/GIH) scream replaceable; a marginal aggressive two-drop you play only when short on bodies.
Step Between Worlds: Trap rare; near-unplayable at 47.8% GIH and a 3% play rate. Symmetrical wheel that refuels your opponent as much as you and costs 3UU or a full plot turn. The +2.8 IWD is noise from a tiny sample. Leave it in the box outside a dedicated draw-go control shell.
Stoic Sphinx: Bomb-adjacent rare — a 5/3 flash flyer for 2UU that's effectively hexproof on your durdle turns, so it closes fast and dodges removal. Elite +9.6 IWD and 60.5% GIH; the flash-flying clock is exactly what UB/UW control wants. High pick, well above its B+ pre-data grade.
Stop Cold: Premium control removal, the UW/UB answer to bombs. Flash exile-lock (loses all abilities, never untaps) neutralizes anything, and exile matters against this set's recursion. GIH underrates it at 53.5% because it's a control card — the 56.3% gd_wr is the real number. Prioritize it in blue.
Take the Fall: Solid blue removal-ish common, best in outlaw decks. With an outlaw it's -4/-0 plus a cantrip — a clean combat blowout that replaces itself; without one it's a weak -1/-0. The +4.6 IWD and 57.7% GD WR reflect the outlaw version; a high pick in UB/BR, a mediocre cantrip elsewhere.
This Town Ain't Big Enough: Excellent blue tempo/control card the community warmed to mid-format. For 1U it's a double-bounce (targeting your own permanent drops the cost), setting up huge tempo swings and re-triggering ETBs. The gap between 49.9% OH and 56.8% GD confirms it's a mid-game weapon, not a keep-in-opener. Prioritize in UW/UB/UR control.
Three Steps Ahead: Premium blue bomb — first-pick territory. A one-mana Spree that counters, copies a creature, or loots-plus, scaling with your mana all game. The 58.4% GIH WR, +8.1 IWD and 2.6 ALSA are elite; the B+ grade undersells it. Take it and play blue.
Visage Bandit: Late-going blue uncommon with a real ceiling — a plotted 2/2 that clones your best creature. The 52.6% GIH WR undersells its UW combo with Wrangler of the Damned (plot it, flash Wrangler, copy for double spirits per LoL). Provisionally a build-around role-player: mediocre as a vanilla clone, strong with ETB fodder.
Ambush Gigapede: One of black's best commons — a two-for-one at instant speed. Flash it end-of-turn to ambush a blocker with -2/-2 (killing most X/2s) then swing with a 6/2. 56.8% GIH and +3.8 iwd back it up; the C grade is too low. The removal-underrating effect is in play here. Solid early-mid pick in any black deck.
Binding Negotiation: Playable disruption but low-impact; more filler than the C-/D grades suggest is bad. Reveal-and-discard a nonland is best on the play or in a UB control mirror, but it does nothing to the board and whiffs late. The 54.9% WR reflects a fine role-player — take it mid-pack in control, cut it from aggro.
Blacksnag Buzzard: Filler flier for black decks. A 2/1 flyer for three that grows only if a creature already died, with plot as a bonus. The 50.6% GIH WR and negative iwd say it's a low-impact evasive body — playable in BR/BW aggro that trades early, but a late pick you can wheel.
Blood Hustler: Solid two-drop for crime decks, a fine early pick in UB/BR. The crime-counter growth plus a late-game lifedrain mana sink gives it reach; 56% GIH and a 92% play rate say it's a reliable inclusion. Not a bomb — it needs a crime density to snowball, but the floor is a serviceable body.
Boneyard Desecrator: Niche sac-outlet role-player for BR/BW aggro — a 3/4 menace that grinds counters and makes Treasure off sacrificed outlaws. 51.1% GIH and a low 27.5% play rate say it's mostly a sideboard/late-deck card; fine if you have expendable outlaws to feed it, otherwise skippable.
Caustic Bronco: Bomb-adjacent two-drop and a first-pick-quality attacker: 63% opening-hand WR and a massive +7.0 IWD. Unsaddled it's a card-advantage Dark Confidant on legs; saddled in a go-wide GW/BW board it drains the opponent instead. Snap it early — it's great in any black deck, best with a wide board.
Consuming Ashes: Premium black removal and a first-picks-priority answer — 2BB exiles ANY creature (crucial vs the format's recursion and bombs) with surveil upside on cheap targets. 57.9% GIH understates it since removal underperforms by being drawn; the exile clause is the whole point. Grab it early in any black deck, especially grindy UB/BW.
Corrupted Conviction: Niche sacrifice payoff, sideboard-y in most decks. One-mana draw-two needs a creature to eat, so it's only good with death triggers or tokens (BW/BR). 52.6% GIH and an 18.5% play rate flag it as a specialist card — don't maindeck without fodder synergy.
Desert's Due: Premium black removal — a core early pick. -2/-2 for two commits a crime and kills most of the curve, scaling further with the ubiquitous crime-deserts, and it recurs off Slickshot Lockpicker. Both LoL and Numot call it strong; GIH underrates efficient removal, so value it above its 57.7%. Prioritize in any black deck.
Desperate Bloodseeker: Above-rate black two-drop. A 2/2 lifelink for 1B is already fine, and the self-mill fuels GB/UB graveyard payoffs (Honest Rutstein, Lively Dirge). 57.0% GIH on 87.6% play is a genuinely good aggressive common — take it as a curve-filler that pulls its weight.
Fake Your Own Death: Above-rate combat trick / blowout. Protects a creature from removal and rebuys it with a Treasure, punishing block-and-kill spots; the doctrine notes the Slickshot Lockpicker combo. Strong 55.3% GIH WR and +2.6 IWD make it a solid UB/BR playable, not just a niche trick.
Forsaken Miner: Solid aggressive black uncommon for BR outlaws — a recurring {B} 2/2 that can't block but keeps coming back every crime. Note the OH WR (58%) well above drawn WR: it's a proactive early beater that's best in your opener. Grindy, resilient two-drop that fuels the crimes-and-sacrifice plans.
Gisa, the Hellraiser: First-pick bomb. Ward protects her, the +1/+1-and-menace anthem is real, and every crime spits out two 2/2s — she snowballs any UB/BR crime board out of reach. 61.5% GIH, +10.4 iwd, ALSA 1.3, 94% play. Take her over almost anything and let removal/crimes flow around her.
Hollow Marauder: Strong UB/graveyard payoff that overperforms its B- grade — 59.6% GIH WR, +6.2 IWD, 92% play rate. In any deck filling its yard it comes down as a cheap 4/2 flyer that strips a card and often refills your hand, a legitimately swingy tempo/value play. High pick in black; the discount makes it a bomb in dedicated GB/UB.
Insatiable Avarice: Trap-adjacent rare; the D grade is right that it's below-rate. Spree tutor-to-top or Night's Whisper-style draw-3-lose-3 is flexible but slow and card-neutral on the tutor mode. The 55.7% drawn WR is soup-inflated by good pilots; in a normal 40 it's a marginal value card, not a bomb — mid-to-late pick in grindy UB/BW.
Kaervek, the Punisher: Overrated rare — the C+ grade is closer than the crime-payoff hype. The recursion engine is powerful in a dedicated UB/BR crime deck, but 52% GIH with a poor 49.6% OH shows a fragile 3/3 that does nothing unless you're already flooded with crimes and black cards in the yard. Playable, not a first pick.
Lively Dirge: Grindy recursion payoff for BW/GB — the {2} mode reanimates two small creatures, a strong two-for-one, and {1} sets up tutors/graveyard fuel. 56.5% GIH with GD (58.8%) well above OH confirms it's a late-game value card, not a tempo play; solid in recursion decks.
Mourner's Surprise: Above-average value common for BW/GB recursion: rebuys your best dead creature and leaves a 1/1 body behind. 58.7% drawn WR and the Harvester of Misery loop (kill, then get it back) push it up. Solid maindeck glue, not a bomb — take it after removal and rate creatures.
Neutralize the Guards: Sideboard / niche only — a mass -1/-1 that reads like a sweeper but only shrinks, rarely kills, and does nothing to a developed board. D grade and a damning 12.8% play rate confirm it; the 52.4% GIH is from the rare go-wide-blowout games. Skip in most black decks.
Nezumi Linkbreaker: Fine one-drop for aggressive black decks (BR outlaws). A 1/1 Warlock that leaves a Mercenary token behind chips in and feeds sacrifice/crime. 55.5% GIH is respectable for a one-drop; it's a role-player that curves and pings, not a card you reach for.
Overzealous Muscle: Filler. A 5/4 for five whose indestructible only fires on your turn after a crime, so it doesn't survive blocks or instant-speed removal reliably — a vanilla beater most of the time. 50% GIH and 27% play rate confirm it's a low-end BR curve-topper you can cut.
Pitiless Carnage: Trap rare — don't play it. 45.3% GIH, -2.6 IWD, 4.4% play rate: sacrificing your board to refill is a losing bargain in a midrange format. Only a dedicated aristocrats shell that doesn't exist here would want it. Cut, sideboard at best.
Rakish Crew: Middling outlaw payoff for BR. Makes a Mercenary token and drains when your outlaws die, but the drain is slow and the 50.8% GIH WR with +0.1 IWD says it barely moves games. A synergy filler in dedicated BR aggro, a cut in anything else.
Rattleback Apothecary: Strong black uncommon and a high pick in crime decks — a 3/2 deathtouch that hands out menace or lifelink on every crime, turning removal spells into evasion or life swings. 86.5% play rate, B grade; deathtouch alone makes it a fine body, and in UB/BR it snowballs each turn.
Raven of Fell Omens: A trap that reads better than it plays — the doctrine flags it as 'understated' but overrated live. A 1/2 flyer that drains 1 per crime (once/turn) is fine incidental value, but you're not building around it. 54.3% GIH is respectable for a two-drop flyer; take it as a solid BR/UB crime role-player, not a payoff to prioritize.
Rictus Robber: Good black common-uncommon; take it fairly early in any B deck. A 4/3 for four that makes a 2/2 whenever anything died — trivially easy in a removal format — and the Plot line lets you double-spell later. 54.9% WR and 86% play rate mark it a reliable midrange body, not a bomb but a clean two-for-one.
Rooftop Assassin: Solid black removal-on-a-body. Flash 2/2 flyer with lifelink that destroys a creature already dealt damage this turn — pairs with any ping, fight, or a chump-block to become a two-for-one at instant speed. The +2.9 iwd and 57% drawn WR back the flexibility; a strong mid-pick in any black deck.
Rush of Dread: Premium black rare and one of the best cards here — 60.2% GIH with a huge +8.3 IWD. The half-your-board edict plus discard plus life-loss modes scale into a blowout, best in grindy UB control per LoL. Spree flexibility means it's never dead. Take it early over most creatures.
Servant of the Stinger: Strong crime two-drop — a 1/3 deathtouch that trades up or blocks all day, and once you've committed a crime it sacs for a tutor. LoL calls it a decent deathtouch body; 56.8% GIH and 89.7% play rate make it a reliable early pick in UB/BR/BW crime decks.
Shoot the Sheriff: Premium removal — treat it as a high pick despite the non-Outlaw clause. GIH underrates it, but the +5.2 IWD and 92% play rate tell the truth: instant-speed destroy for 1B answers the format's best deck (GW Mounts aren't Outlaws) and most bombs. Grab it over most creatures.
Skulduggery: Doctrine says don't play it — the retrospective calls it "absolute trash." A one-shot +1/-1 combat trick that needs two creatures on board and swings only two points; 53.1% GIH is inflated by combat blowouts. The 48.7% play rate is already too high. Leave it in the sideboard.
Tinybones Joins Up: Trap rare — leave it in the binder. A one-mana discard that needs a legendary-creature critical mass to mill/drain does little in a normal 40. 49.3% GIH and a 13.2% play rate confirm it's a build-around that rarely comes together; unplayable most decks.
Tinybones, the Pickpocket: Strong one-drop, near-first-pickable in black. A deathtouch 1/1 that trades up all day and, once it connects, steals castable cards from their yard — real evasion-adjacent value. ALSA 2.0 and 88% play rate show it's a premium early grab; slot it in any black deck and enable the damage.
Treasure Dredger: Playable fixing/ramp two-drop, roughly on-rate. A 2/2 that slowly makes Treasures smooths splashes and enables the 4-5c good-stuff pile, but activating it costs mana and life, so it's a role-player not a bomb. 53.4% GIH is a fine floor; take it higher if you're going greedy on colors.
Unfortunate Accident: Premium black removal — high pick. Spree gives you unconditional creature destruction that can also spit out a Mercenary token, so it's flexible and always live. The 57.4% GIH WR, +4.5 IWD and 3.1 ALSA confirm top-tier; GIH underrates efficient removal, so value it even higher.
Unscrupulous Contractor: Good black uncommon and flexible value — a 3/2 that turns a spare creature into draw-two-lose-2, with plot for a double-spell turn later. The sac is a bonus, not a requirement, so it's never a dead card; sits comfortably in any black deck, best with tokens or dying creatures to feed it.
Vadmir, New Blood: Strong two-drop that snowballs in a crime deck. Grows every turn you commit a crime and gains menace+lifelink at four counters, becoming a fast clock. ALSA 1.8 and 93% play show it's picked highly, but the modest +5.8 iwd / 57.9% GIH mark it as a good build-around, not a slam bomb. Early pick in BR/UB crime.
Vault Plunderer: Premium common — near-unconditional card draw on a body, take it highly. A 3/1 for {2}{B} that draws you a card and pings for one is efficient value in a grindy format; LoL wanted four copies. 57.9% GIH WR and 91% play rate back it up. Excellent in every black deck, the glue of UB/BR grind.
Brimstone Roundup: Below-rate build-around, essentially a trap. Needs a second-spell-per-turn cadence to make 1/1 Mercenaries, and the tokens are weak — the 47.8% GIH WR and 26.3% play rate say it underdelivers. Only consider it in a dedicated UR/BR spells-matter deck; otherwise leave it.
Calamity, Galloping Inferno: Bomb-adjacent red rare, first-pickable. A 4/6 haste for six that copies your saddling attackers doubles your board damage in combat, and saddle 1 is trivial to turn on. 55.5% GIH understates the ceiling in go-wide RW/RG. The 1.7 ALSA confirms nobody passes it.
Caught in the Crossfire: Trap sweeper — a double-red spree that deals only 2 to a chosen creature type, awkward to aim and weak against the format's bigger bodies. 48.6% GIH, -2.0 iwd, and a 19.1% play rate all confirm it underperforms; sideboard-only against wide low-toughness boards.
Cunning Coyote: Good tempo two-drop for RG/RW aggro: a 2/2 haste that hands another creature +1/+1 and haste, and can flash in via plot to ambush or save a creature. Numot notes it wrecks combat with a board. 54.6% GIH is fine for a red common-adjacent uncommon; solid, not premium.
Deadeye Duelist: Filler two-drop — a 1/3 reach body that pings for 1 with a mana investment, so it blocks fliers and grinds a little reach damage. C- and a flat -0.1 IWD say it's replacement-level; playable defensive glue in BR/RW aggro but never a card you want to prioritize.
Demonic Ruckus: Solid aggressive aura, plays in BR/RW aggro. +1/+1 with menace and trample plus a card back when it dies makes it low-risk, and the plot line adds reach. 53.1% GIH and 52% play rate are fine for an aura; a reliable role-player that pushes damage without card disadvantage.
Discerning Peddler: Filler two-drop. A 2/2 that loots on ETB — fine card smoothing and a Rogue for outlaw synergies, but the -0.1 IWD and 53.8% GIH mark it as a replaceable body. Playable in BR/UB when you want the outlaw type and graveyard fuel; nothing to prioritize.
Explosive Derailment: Premium red removal and a two-for-one — one of red's best commons. 4 damage kills most things and the artifact mode adds reach; LoL flags the two-for-one upside and Ben doubled up in Early Access. B grade with 54.7% GIH underrates it because efficient removal doesn't win by being drawn. High pick in any red deck.
Ferocification: Marginal aggro enabler. A repeatable combat-step pump granting +2/+0 or menace+haste can push damage, but it's card-disadvantageous and does nothing on an empty board; 50.3% GIH WR and negative IWD make it a fringe RW/RG aggro card despite the C+ grade.
Gila Courser: Above-average red uncommon and a fine aggressive Mount — a 4/2 for three that generates card advantage whenever it connects while saddled. Note the ~0 IWD: it wants a developed board to saddle, so it's a curve-filler that rewards go-wide, not a card you're happy drawing late. Solid RW/RG playable.
Great Train Heist: Build-around finisher for go-wide aggro, not a generic playable. The extra-combat-plus-firststrike mode ends games from a real board — Numot: 'round-one victory' with 5+ power creatures. But 53.8% GIH and the fact that it does nothing without a board keep it honest. High pick specifically in RW/GW go-wide; mediocre elsewhere.
Hell to Pay: Premium scalable removal; high pick in any red deck. {X}{R} kills nearly any creature and the excess damage makes Treasures, so it doubles as ramp/fixing in the mid-late game. 51.6% GIH WR reads low but that's the removal-underrating effect — the 3.0 ALSA and 83% play rate show players correctly prize it. Flexible, splash-friendly answer.
Hellspur Brute: Strong payoff for BR outlaws aggro — LoL: good in all-outlaw red. A 5/4 trample for 4R that costs {1} less per outlaw you control, so it lands turn 3-4 in the aggressive shell. The 77% play rate and B- grade are the built-around number; outside BR outlaws it's just a clunky five-drop.
Hellspur Posse Boss: Premium red rare, an A-level bomb — 61.8% GIH and +9.3 IWD are elite. A 2/4 that grants your outlaws haste and immediately makes two Mercenary tokens that pump the team is a go-wide, aggro-defining threat. Slam it in any BR/RW/RG build; it wins the games it's drawn.
Highway Robbery: The engine that powers UR/blue-red late-game decks — a cheap card-filtering draw-two with plot for a free future double-spell turn. LoL loves it, but 52.0% GIH and negative iwd show it's a build-around, not a slam: prioritize it only when you're the control/double-spell deck.
Irascible Wolverine: Filler-plus red common: a 3/2 for 2R with a card-advantage ETB (impulse-draw the top card) and plot flexibility. The negative -1.2 IWD says it's a curve-filler you play, not one you want to draw late. Fine body for RW/BR aggro but nothing to prioritize.
Iron-Fist Pulverizer: Niche five-drop payoff — a 4/5 reach that rewards a dedicated double-spell turn with 2 reach damage plus scry. The C grade and low 29.5% play rate reflect that most decks can't reliably cast two spells a turn; wants UR/Izzet spells-matter. Fine top-end there, filler elsewhere.
Longhorn Sharpshooter: High pick — removal stapled to a body. A 3/3 reach that deals 2 to any target when plotted is a two-for-one you cast on curve then replay for free. 56.9% GIH, +3.7 IWD, and a 3.1 ALSA make it one of red's best commons/uncommons; grab it early.
Magda, the Hoardmaster: Bomb-adjacent rare, high pick. A 2/2 for two that turns your removal-heavy crime deck into a Treasure engine, then converts three Treasures into a 4/4 flying haste Dragon — ramp, fixing, and a win-con on one card. ALSA 1.8 and 91% play rate; snap it up in any red crime deck (BR/UR/RG).
Magebane Lizard: Trap/sideboard only. 46.3% GIH, -5.4 IWD, 8.5% play — a 1/4 wall whose spell-punish ability rarely matters and is symmetric against you. It does nothing to a creature deck. Leave it in the board unless you're facing a spell-heavy opponent.
Mine Raider: Playable outlaw common. A 3/2 trampler that ramps a Treasure when you already have an outlaw — fine aggressive body with light upside for BR. The 51.7% GIH WR is average, so it's a serviceable curve-filler rather than a card to prioritize.
Outlaws' Fury: Trap-adjacent combat trick — team +2/+0 with a card off the top if you have an outlaw. 15% play rate and negative IWD confirm it's a narrow all-in aggro card (LoL: Razzle-Dazzler decks). Skip unless you're a fully-built low-curve BR/RW go-wide deck; even then it's a risky blowout-or-bust.
Prickly Pair: Quietly excellent common — two bodies for three mana that pump the team. B grade tracks better than the flat 54.5% GIH; the extra Mercenary enables saddle, chump-blocks, and repeatable +1/+0 for combat math. Solid early pick in any red go-wide deck (RW/RG/BR), better than its stat line suggests.
Quick Draw: Sideboard/combat trick filler. A one-mana first-strike pump that also strips their double/first strike is a blowout in the right combat, but it's a do-nothing card that needs a board — 9.6% play rate, 8.3 ALSA. Keep one for aggressive RW/BR mirrors; not a maindeck default despite the C+ grade.
Quilled Charger: Filler Mount, a role-player at best. A 4/3 for four that gets +1/+2 and menace when saddled, but requires a go-wide board to saddle. The 51.6% GIH WR, negative iwd, and 38.7% play rate mark it as a replaceable body — a late pick even in GW/RW Mounts.
Reckless Lackey: Role-player one-drop for aggressive BR/RW. First strike haste is a real early poke, and the sac-for-card-and-Treasure keeps it from being a late-game blank. But 52% GIH and a 44% play rate mean it's a filler two-drop-slot enabler, not a priority — only wanted when your outlaw-aggro curve needs bodies.
Resilient Roadrunner: Serviceable aggressive two-drop — a 2/2 haste that can pseudo-unblockable itself for {3} in the late game. 53.7% GIH and a flat iwd mark it as a fine curve-filler for red aggro (BR/RW), nothing more; a role-player you're happy to run but never prioritize.
Return the Favor: Sideboard card, not a maindeck card — the 48.2% GIH and 17% play rate say it plainly. Copying a spell or redirecting removal needs a target-rich matchup; Numot flagged it as strong in BO3 sideboards specifically. Don't main it; hold for the mirror or against bombs.
Rodeo Pyromancers: Below replacement — a 3/4 for 3R whose ritual only matters in a build-around big-mana shell, and even then it's fragile. 47.8% GIH and 14.8% play rate are both red flags. The vanilla stats are okay but the payoff rarely fires; leave it out of normal red decks.
Scalestorm Summoner: Strong RG/RW aggro two-drop. A 3/3 that spawns a 3/1 Dino each attack once you have a 4-power creature snowballs the board fast. 57.6% oh_wr shows it wants to be curving into big bodies; 55.6% GIH and a 3.8 ALSA make it a solid early pick in stompy/go-wide red.
Scorching Shot: Premium red removal. Five damage for RR kills nearly everything in the format at instant-relevant speed for a sorcery, and the double-pip is the only real cost. B grade and 54% GIH understate it — GIH lowballs removal — so pick it early in any red deck.
Slickshot Show-Off: Strong aggressive rare, take it early. Flying haste for 1R with pump-on-noncreature-spell plus Plot flexibility gives reach and a fast clock in any red aggro (BR/UR/RW). The 52.1% GIH is deflated because it wants a spell-dense deck; in the right build the 2.6 ALSA and B+ grade are the truer read.
Stingerback Terror: Bomb — first-pick. A 7/7 flying trampler for four that plots to dodge the empty-hand drawback, so you dump your hand then unload it for free as an evasive haymaker. Elite 59.1% GIH WR, +6.3 IWD, 1.7 ALSA and A- grade all agree.
Take for a Ride: Niche red uncommon — a Threaten that gains flash after a crime, best paired with a sac outlet to keep the stolen creature. 28% play rate and negative IWD flag it as a tempo/combo piece, not maindeck removal. A sideboard-to-situational card for crime decks with sac; otherwise leave it.
Terror of the Peaks: Format-warping bomb — pick it over nearly everything. A 5/4 flyer that's hard to target and pings any target for each subsequent creature's power, turning every follow-up into removal or reach. 59.9% GIH, +9.3 iwd, ALSA 1.3, A grade. In a creature deck this ends games on its own.
Thunder Salvo: Solid red removal and a fine early-mid pick. Base 2 damage for {1}{R} kills most 2-drops, and it scales in any double-spell or spell-heavy UR/BR turn to finish bigger threats. 53.3% WR with 71% play rate is good for removal (which GIH underrates). Efficient, mostly maindeckable answer — take it over most red creatures.
Trick Shot: Sizeable but overcosted removal; a playable role-player. 4R for 6 damage to a creature (plus 2 to a token) kills almost anything but is slow at five mana and dead against no board. The 27.2% play rate reflects the cost; solid in slower red decks that need a hard answer, otherwise a mid-late pick.
Aloe Alchemist: Strong green uncommon, an early pick — a 3/2 trample for two with an upside line: plotting it pumps a creature +3/+2 with trample, effectively a combat trick that also becomes a free body later. 57.5% GIH, 93% play rate. Flexible tempo-and-value in any green deck, especially RG/GW.
Ankle Biter: Playable one-drop for green decks — a 1/1 deathtouch that trades up against anything and gates attacks early. 54.1% GIH is respectable for a one-drop but the negative iwd shows it doesn't win games alone; a fine early body and saddle-fuel in GW go-wide, a filler elsewhere.
Beastbond Outcaster: Excellent green uncommon and an early pick: a 3/3 for 2G that draws a card if you have a power-4 body, which green fills easily, plus plot flexibility to double-spell. 59% opening-hand WR, +3.0 IWD, 93% play rate. Reliable curve-and-card-advantage in any green deck.
Betrayal at the Vault: Solid green removal that plays like a double-fight — point your fattie's power at two of their creatures for one card, a strong two-for-one in RG/GW stompy where you have big bodies. 56.4% GIH; six mana and needing a beefy attacker is the catch, but it's a real answer. Good mid pick.
Bristlepack Sentry: Efficient green common, best in RG stompy. A 3/3 defender for two blocks everything early and swings once you control a 4-power creature. 55.1% GIH with slightly negative IWD reflects a defensive floor; a fine curve-filler that turns aggressive in a big-creature deck.
Bristly Bill, Spine Sower: Bomb. A two-mana legend that snowballs every landfall into a counter and then doubles ALL your counters for GG — it takes over any board it's left on. 63.5% GIH, +9.7 IWD, ALSA 1.3: a first-pick that anchors green, elite in GW/RG counters. Take it over almost anything.
Cactarantula: Reliable green beater and a fine floor. A 6/5 reach that costs 3GG (or less with a Desert) that cantrips when targeted — hard for opponents to remove cleanly. 56.7% GIH on 90.8% play is a solid midrange body; not exciting but a dependable top-end in any green deck, especially with deserts.
Colossal Rattlewurm: Green bomb — first-pick. A 6/5 trampler with flash whenever you control a Desert, plus graveyard Desert-ramp that fixes and turns on desert synergies. Flashing this in as a blocker or ambush is backbreaking; 60.9% GIH WR and 1.5 ALSA confirm elite. Rewards desert/RG decks.
Dance of the Tumbleweeds: Underrated green common — a spree that ramps/fixes ({1}: fetch a land or Desert) and later makes a huge Elemental. LoL: 'looks innocuous but is actually quite strong.' Numot's ramp enabler for RG stompy, but the fixing mode alone makes it a fine early play that scales into a threat late.
Drover Grizzly: Fine aggressive two-power-per-mana beater, best in a Mounts shell. 4/2 for three that grants team trample when saddled — real reach in GW/RG go-wide. But it's fragile and the negative iwd (-1.1) plus C- grade show it's a body you play, not prioritize. The 55.1% GIH is deck-context; solid role-player, mid pick.
Freestrider Commando: Below-average green common; a role-player. As a hardcast 3/3 for {2}{G} it's vanilla, and the -1.2 IWD confirms it does nothing when drawn late. Its trick is Plotting it, then it enters as a 5/5 for free — a nice value line but slow. Playable curve-filler in green, not a card you prioritize.
Freestrider Lookout: Excellent green rare and a near-first-pick — ALSA 1.9, 92% play rate. A 3/3 reach for three that ramps/fixes every time you commit a crime, which every removal spell triggers. Fits GB/RG value and any crime deck; the +2.6 iwd and 56.3% WR are legit, not soup-inflated. Take it early.
Full Steam Ahead: Situational green finisher, not a maindeck staple — 53.9% GIH but a telling 34% play rate. The team +2/+2 trample with near-unblockable is a go-wide GW/RG blowout, but it's dead when you're behind and clunky at 3GG. A sideboard-in / late-pick that rewards a wide board only.
Giant Beaver: Excellent-rate common and an early pick for GW/RG — a 3G 4/4 vigilance Mount that grows your attackers when saddled, per LoL an efficient body. 55.7% GIH with a strong 4.0 ALSA and 92.4% play rate; a reliable midrange beater that blocks and attacks, high on the green pick order.
Gold Rush: Middling green trick: makes a Treasure (ramp/fixing) and pumps based on Treasures, so it usually reads +4/+4 in combat. Negative -1.0 IWD marks it as a do-nothing when drawn late. The Treasure floor gives it a role in ramp/splash builds, but it's a filler combat trick.
Goldvein Hydra: Bomb — an X-spell 0/0 with vigilance, trample, AND haste that swings the turn it lands and refunds Treasure on death, so it's never a blowout to remove. Elite 1.3 ALSA and 59.5% GIH; scalable, evasive-ish, and ramps you. First-pick material in any green deck.
Hardbristle Bandit: Good green two-drop that fixes and untaps on crimes. A 1/1 mana dork ramps you and enables splashes/deserts, and 91.3% play rate plus 59.1% oh_wr show it's a near-auto include. The 55.8% GIH is solid; take it as ramp/fixing that keeps you open, especially in crime shells.
Intrepid Stablemaster: Strong green two-drop, high pick in GW. A 2/2 reach ramp body that fixes and accelerates Mounts/Vehicles — enables your bomb Mounts a turn early while blocking fliers. 93% play rate and B grade; a reliable early pick that's great in Mounts and fine as a mana dork anywhere green.
Map the Frontier: Filler ramp/fixing, mostly for the 4-5c pile. Fetching two tapped lands (basics or Deserts) enables greedy splashes and desert payoffs, but -1.8 IWD and 28.7% play say it's too slow for normal green decks. Only worth it when your deck genuinely needs the fixing.
Ornery Tumblewagg: Bomb — first-pick, especially GW. A 3-mana Mount that snowballs +1/+1 counters every combat and DOUBLES them when saddled, ending games fast in a go-wide shell. Absurd 62.7% GIH WR, +9.1 IWD, 1.4 ALSA and 64.8% OH WR make it one of the best cards in the set.
Outcaster Greenblade: Premium green uncommon — 'probably the best uncommon in the set.' A 1/2 that fetches a Desert to hand and grows +1/+1 per Desert you control, so it fixes AND becomes a threat. 61.4% GIH WR with +6.5 IWD is elite; a high pick that pushes you toward Desert-rich green/multicolor. Take it early.
Outcaster Trailblazer: Premium green rare — ramp, fixing, and a card-advantage engine on a 4/2. ETB any-color mana smooths your curve, and it draws whenever a 4-power creature enters, which green does constantly. Plot gives flexibility. 59.4% GIH, ALSA 1.6, B+ grade. Early pick in any green deck, especially GW/RG stompy.
Patient Naturalist: The set's famous green-common trap — good stats, wrong role. 56.7% WR looks premier, but Retro/Hosst are firm it's "not what you're trying to do": mill-3-for-a-land is fixing/filler that sits below the green rate creatures. Fine playable and a nice enabler for GB/GU, just don't take it over Throw from the Saddle or real bodies.
Railway Brawler: Set-defining bomb and a slam first pick — 65.2% GIH WR, +12.5 iwd, ALSA 1.2, Numot's #1 mythic. A 5/5 reach/trample that turns every subsequent creature into a monster, single-handedly winning RG stompy. Plot lets you deploy it safely. First-pick it every time and move into green.
Rambling Possum: Good green Mount uncommon, B+ theory backed by a fine 89.9% play rate — a 3/3 for three that saddles into a 4/5 and bounces your own ETB creatures for extra value. Solid GW/RG go-wide role-player; the flat IWD shows it's a curve-filler beater, not a bomb.
Raucous Entertainer: Build-around anthem for GW go-wide/counters — taps to pump every creature that entered that turn, snowballing a flood board. The negative iwd (-2.2) shows it's mediocre when drawn late off-plan, but the B grade and 84.6% play rate reflect its ceiling; solid in the right deck, filler otherwise.
Reach for the Sky: Below-average aura, sideboard/filler: +3/+2 and reach at flash speed with a draw when it dies, so it's not pure card disadvantage, but auras get blown out and the 25% play rate reflects that. 55.5% GIH is soft. Fine anti-flyer tech; don't prioritize.
Rise of the Varmints: Build-around uncommon for graveyard-stuffed green decks — makes a token per creature in your yard, so it's a blowout in grindy GB/GW but a dead card early. The plot option smooths that. 54.2% GIH but a stark +6.6pp OH-to-GD split flags it as a late/synergy payoff, not a slam.
Smuggler's Surprise: Flexible green rare, a solid pick in creature-heavy decks. Spree modes dig, cheat fatties in, or protect your board — always useful, never dead. 57.2% GIH and 58.5% gd_wr with a 3.0 ALSA make it a reliable value spell; the C grade undersells it, trust the live number.
Snakeskin Veil: Above-rate protection trick. One mana to counter removal and permanently grow a creature — protects your bombs and wins combat, exactly what a counters/aura deck wants. 57.2% GIH is strong for a trick; solid in GW/RG, but it's a two-for-nothing when you're behind, so don't over-draft copies.
Spinewoods Armadillo: Green bomb-adjacent uncommon — high pick. A 7/7 reach with Ward 3 is nearly impossible to answer, and the discard-to-tutor-a-land mode makes it never a dead card. 60.5% GIH, +5.8 IWD, 2.3 ALSA: it overperforms and goes early. Best in GW/RG stompy but great in any green deck.
Spinewoods Paladin: Solid green common. A 5/4 trampler gaining 3 life is a fine top-end body; the plot mode is mostly irrelevant (LoL: "never really wanting to plot this"), just hardcast it. Strong 57.3% GIH WR and B grade make it a reliable green playable you're happy to run.
Stubborn Burrowfiend: Strong green two-drop Mount — a 2/2 that mills two and grows by your graveyard's creature count each time it's saddled, so it hits hard on turn three onward. 92% play rate, note OH WR above drawn (a proactive beater). Excellent aggressive GW/GB curve-filler that snowballs with a go-wide board.
Throw from the Saddle: The best common in the set (LoL, retro) and premium removal — grab it early. A fight spell with a built-in pump that becomes a permanent counter on Mounts, killing most things while advancing your board. 58.9% GIH understates it because efficient removal doesn't win by being drawn. Core to every green deck; prioritize over most uncommons.
Trash the Town: Premium green combat spell — take it early in any green deck. For {G} base it's a flexible Spree: +2/+2 counters, trample, and a Curiosity mode that can refill your whole hand off one hit. 58.3% GIH WR and 90% play rate; scales from a cheap pump to a game-ending, card-drawing swing. Among the best green uncommons.
Tumbleweed Rising: Solid green payoff in go-wide, a good mid-pick. 1G makes an X/X where X is your greatest power — snowballs hard once you've got a fatty, and plot enables a double-spell turn. The 55.8% WR is real but conditional on board presence; best in GW/RG. Flat if cast on an empty board.
Voracious Varmint: Filler green common that doubles as artifact/enchantment removal — a 2/2 vigilance you can sacrifice to blow up an Equipment, Torpor Orb, or problem aura. 54.8% GIH is fine, but the C- grade and negative IWD flag it as a replaceable body. Nice flexibility, low priority.
Akul the Unrepentant: Strong bomb-adjacent rare for BR sacrifice — a 5/5 flying trample for four that cheats creatures from hand by eating three bodies. 53.9% GIH is modest because it wants a sac-heavy board, but B+ grade and +3.9 iwd say it closes games; high pick when you're the BR/BW go-wide sacrifice deck.
Annie Flash, the Veteran: Bomb — take it P1P1 in any WRG-reachable seat. A 4/5 flash that reanimates a 3-drop on entry and impulse-draws two every time it taps (attack or block). A-grade, 61% drawn WR, +5.9 IWD. Three-color cost is the only cost of entry; the fixing is worth it.
Annie Joins Up: Removal-plus-engine rare, but demanding on mana (Naya, 1RGW) — the ETB 5 damage is a clean kill and playable alone, while the legendary-double payoff is gravy you rarely fully use. 53.2% GIH and flat IWD say it's mostly a five-damage removal spell in practice; solid if you're already RGW, otherwise passable.
Assimilation Aegis: Bomb — one of the best UW cards. ETB exiles a creature (removal), then equip turns your guy into a copy of it, so it's answer plus threat in one, and re-equipping resets the exile. +5.6 IWD and 56.7% GIH with a 2.6 ALSA scream first-pick in any WU direction.
At Knifepoint: Mid BR uncommon, synergy-gated. First strike plus a crime-triggered token engine rewards a wide outlaw board, but a three-mana do-nothing-immediately enchantment is slow — the 50.6% GIH and +0.5 IWD show it underdelivers. Playable payoff in dedicated BR aggro; a low pick that you don't splash for.
Badlands Revival: Strong BW/GB recursion payoff. Reanimating a creature AND returning a permanent for 3BG is a two-for-one that shines with big ETBs and grind. The OH/GD split (52.3 vs 58.8) shows it's a mid-to-late value card, not a keep. 56.3% GIH is real in a deck with good targets — prioritize in GB midrange.
Baron Bertram Graywater: Strong BW signpost uncommon. Spins tokens into lifelink Vampires and turns spare permanents into cards via the sac-draw engine — real grind value. The 54.0% GIH WR and B grade back a high pick in BW midrange/tokens; centerpiece for that pair.
Bonny Pall, Clearcutter: Format-defining bomb — first-pick over almost anything. A 6/5 reach for six that makes a land-sized Ox and, on every attack, draws a card plus ramps a land. 66.4% GIH WR and a staggering +16.1 IWD; if you open it, you're GU/Simic base. Wins the game on its own if unanswered.
Breeches, the Blastmaker: A-grade on paper, but the live data screams trap outside a dedicated artifact/spellslinger deck — 50.0% GIH, 33% play. You need cheap artifacts to sacrifice and a second spell every turn to get the coin-flip value. In a built UR artifacts shell it's a bomb; in a random deck it's a 3/3 menace. Speculative, deck-dependent pick.
Bruse Tarl, Roving Rancher: Bomb — one of the best gold rares, take it over almost anything. A 4/3 for four that generates a 2/2 Ox or a free spell every attack, and turns those Oxen (plus Bovine tokens) into double strikers. 61.2% GIH WR, +8.0 IWD, 2.2 ALSA. Snowballs any RW/GW go-wide board instantly; first-pick quality.
Cactusfolk Sureshot: Strong RG stompy uncommon and a high pick in the pair. A 4/4 reach with ward 2 for four is already good stats, and it hands trample + haste to your other 4-power creatures, which RG produces in bulk. The +3.3 iwd and 57.6% WR confirm it; a beating alongside Railway Brawler.
Congregation Gryff: Premium GW signpost uncommon and a high pick in the best archetype — a 1/4 flying lifelink that saddles into a game-swinging X/X where X is your Mounts. 57.9% GIH understates it in a dedicated Mounts board. The defensive body blocks fliers even when not attacking. Prioritize when GW.
Doc Aurlock, Grizzled Genius: Build-around cost-reducer for GU/plot decks — makes graveyard, exile, and plot spells {2} cheaper, enabling double-spell turns. 52.9% GIH and a 46% play rate show it's replaceable outside its shell; a fine early GU pick but don't overrate it as a generic 2/3.
Eriette, the Beguiler: Powerful but narrow build-around rare: a 4/4 lifelink that steals permanents when your Auras land on them, needing an Aura package (Mystical Tether, Reach for the Sky) to fully break open. The 10% play rate and low opening-hand WR show it's a payoff, not a slam; the inflated 57% drawn WR is the built-around number. Speculative WUB pick.
Ertha Jo, Frontier Mentor: Strong RW uncommon and a build-around engine — copies every targeted activated ability, which turns pump/removal activations and her own Mercenary token into two-for-ones. 56.0% GIH and B grade; a genuine payoff for a go-wide Boros deck with activated abilities. High pick in RW, fine midrange body elsewhere.
Form a Posse: Solid RW go-wide payoff and combat trick in one. X 1/1s that can pump each other flood the board and enable saddle/mass buffs; instant speed lets you ambush. 54.1% GIH is deck-dependent, but in Boros aggro the B+ grade holds — a strong go-wide enabler, mediocre elsewhere.
Ghired, Mirror of the Wilds: Build-around Naya mythic, provisional slam. A 3/3 haste that copies tokens is a bomb in a token-heavy WRG go-wide deck but a fragile three-color three-drop otherwise, and the 44% play rate with 54% GIH reflects that fixing tax. Take it if you're already Naya tokens; otherwise it's a speculative pick.
The Gitrog, Ravenous Ride: First-pick bomb. A 6/5 trample haste Mount with Saddle 1 that draws-and-ramps on connection is an immediate threat that snowballs — 60.0% GIH, +7.7 IWD, 1.5 ALSA. Slam it; it slots into any green deck and is elite in GW/GB/RG. A-grade is if anything conservative.
Honest Rutstein: Premium GB/Abzan gold uncommon — high pick. A 3/2 that rebuys a creature from your graveyard and discounts all future creatures, anchoring green-black recursion value. LoL calls it a standout; 58.4% GIH WR, +4.7 IWD and 3.1 ALSA confirm. The recursion is the GB game plan.
Intimidation Campaign: Signpost payoff for UB crimes — a cantrip-plus-drain enchantment that bounces itself on any crime to re-trigger endlessly. LoL: 'goes very late but incredible once you're in the deck.' The 54.9% GIH WR is deflated by non-crime pilots; the gap between drawn and OH WR confirms it's an engine. Take it and build UB around it.
Jem Lightfoote, Sky Explorer: Good UW payoff — a 3/3 flyer with vigilance that draws whenever you don't cast from hand, rewarding plot and holding up instants. The B grade beats the 51.7% GIH because the card advantage compounds in the control shell it wants. Strong role-player anchoring UW tempo/control; mid-early pick when the pair is open.
Jolene, Plundering Pugilist: Strong RG signpost and a high uncommon pick. A 4/2 for three that fits stompy's power-4 theme, making a Treasure on every big attack that fuels ramp AND a repeatable 1-damage ping to clear blockers or finish. 56.4% WR. Best in RG Railway/stompy but a fine aggressive body anywhere in red-green.
Kambal, Profiteering Mayor: Strong BW rare, a high pick for the token-midrange pair. A 2/4 for three that drains on your token ETBs and steals copies of opponents' tokens — grindy value that pulls ahead over a long game. The +4.3 iwd and 67.8% play rate are solid; best in BW go-wide/crime, playable in any WB.
Kellan Joins Up: Trap rare — the D grade and awful 41.8% GIH (with -4.6 IWD, 4.7% play rate) are damning. It's a three-color GWU enchantment that does almost nothing unless you chain legendary creatures, which no Limited deck reliably does. Effectively unplayable; leave it in the pack.
Kellan, the Kid: Powerful three-color mythic signpost for WUG value — a 3/3 flying lifelink that free-casts permanents off plot/reanimation or ramps a land. +5.9 iwd and 55.4% GIH are strong given the fixing tax; a high pick if you're already in Bant, but the color cost keeps it out of most decks.
Kraum, Violent Cacophony: Strong UR signpost and an early pick for the double-spell control plan: a 2/3 flyer that grows and draws every time you cast your second spell each turn. +5.0 IWD backs it. This is the good UR — late-game value, not Razzle-Dazzler aggro. Prioritize it and build to cast two spells a turn.
Laughing Jasper Flint: Bomb and the BR aggro signpost — a 4/3 for 3 that steals cards off the top scaling with your outlaw count, generating a snowballing advantage. LoL: "broken on turn 3, run it out early, don't hold it." Elite 1.8 ALSA and +7.1 IWD. Slam it and cast it immediately.
Lazav, Familiar Stranger: Strong UB crimes payoff and signpost. A 1/4 that grows and clones graveyard creatures on every crime is a resilient value engine, and you commit crimes for free with removal. 54.8% GIH plus +4.1 IWD is the crime-deck number; prioritize it when UB is open, mediocre outside it.
Lilah, Undefeated Slickshot: Strong UR payoff rare. Prowess plus free-plotting your multicolored spells generates huge card advantage in a spells-matter shell, exactly the late-game UR control plan the doctrine prefers over Razzle aggro. B+ grade and +4.8 IWD; a high pick in UR, but she needs gold instants/sorceries to shine, so read your signals.
Make Your Own Luck: Good UG value/selection uncommon. Digging three deep and plotting a nonland card is card advantage plus a free future spell — a fine engine for the GU self-mill/value pile. 55.9% GIH with the usual OH/GD split marks it as a mid-game card; a solid pickup once you're in GU or a plot-heavy build.
Malcolm, the Eyes: Strong UR payoff — high pick. A 2/2 flying haste that investigates on your second spell each turn, building card advantage in a double-spell shell. The +7.5 IWD and B+ grade are excellent; the 56.3% GIH WR is the built-around number, so it wants UR control, not a random deck.
Marchesa, Dealer of Death: Strong UB-crimes rare and card-advantage engine — a 3/4 for three colors that filters two cards deep on every crime for {1}. The 54.3% GIH WR is the built-around number, inflated for crime-dense pilots and mediocre otherwise; +5.2 IWD shows the ceiling. A high pick that commits you to Grixis/UB crimes.
Miriam, Herd Whisperer: Signpost uncommon for the S-tier GW Mounts deck and a genuine build-around payoff. Two-mana 3/2 that makes your Mounts/Vehicles hexproof on your turn (dodging removal in a removal-heavy format) and grows them on attack. 58.7% GIH with a strong 60.3% OH. High pick that commits you to GW go-wide.
Obeka, Splitter of Seconds: Provisional read (null WR, C grade): a build-around trap in Limited. Extra upkeeps do nothing on their own — you need upkeep payoffs and to connect with a 2/5 menace body, which is unreliable. The 2.2% play rate says drafters correctly pass it. Sideboard/cube fodder; leave it unless you're forced three-color.
Oko, the Ringleader: Bomb planeswalker and a slam early pick — 58.7% GIH WR, +7.8 iwd, ALSA 1.4, 90% play rate. Protects itself by copying a creature, +1 draws two (crime softens the discard), -1 makes 3/3 Elks. Splashable value even outside UG; the crime synergy just sweetens it. First-pickable.
Pillage the Bog: Playable GB card-selection, a middling pick. Digging up to twice-your-lands deep for the best card is real advantage in a grindy Golgari deck, and plot lets you bank it. But it's a two-mana do-nothing-to-the-board dig; 54.9% GIH and 50% play rate say role-player, not staple.
Rakdos Joins Up: Powerful BR value rare — reanimates a creature with two +1/+1 counters on ETB (immediate two-for-one) then pings opponents when your legends die. GD 55.9% well above OH 50.6% marks it a midgame value swing, not a fast play; a strong pick in BR/Rakdos midrange, B+ earned.
Rakdos, the Muscle: Format-warping bomb — arguably the best card in this chunk. 64% GIH, a staggering +13.8 IWD, 92% play rate. A 6/5 flyer/trample that's hard to kill (sac for indestructible) and steals cards off the sacrificed creature's value. First-pick and build BR around it.
Riku of Many Paths: Trap-ish rare — the Temur modal payoff is real only if your deck is stuffed with Spree/modal spells, which most aren't, and the 3/3 body does nothing on its own. 49.1% GIH and a tiny 13.8% play rate confirm it underdelivers; the C+ grade is generous. Skip unless deeply built around it.
Roxanne, Starfall Savant: Format-defining bomb, first-pick over almost anything. Each ETB/attack makes a Meteorite that pings 2 AND ramps, generating removal, mana, and inevitability. 64.2% GIH, +11.1 IWD, 1.7 ALSA — elite. Take it and move into RG; even splashed it wins games on its own.
Ruthless Lawbringer: Premium BW uncommon, splashable. Sac a creature to destroy any nonland permanent is unconditional removal on a 3/2 body — answers bombs and enchantments, and LoL calls it a "late-format powerhouse." 58.2% GIH understates removal; a high pick that goes in most black decks, elite in BW sacrifice.
Satoru, the Infiltrator: Strong UB tempo/crime rare, better than the number reads. Menace 2/3 for UU that cantrips off free/uncast creatures (tokens, blink, saddle) — +4.6 IWD shows it pulls weight. The 54.0% GIH and 57.5% play are build-dependent; in a UB deck with cheap bodies and token-makers it's a high pick.
Selvala, Eager Trailblazer: Bomb mythic — first-pick GW. A 4/5 vigilance that spawns a Mercenary on every creature cast and ramps big colored mana off power diversity. Dominant 62.0% GIH WR, +9.3 IWD, 1.5 ALSA and 63.5% OH WR; slams into the best archetype in the format.
Seraphic Steed: Excellent GW bomb-rare — a 2/2 first-strike lifelink Mount that spits out a 3/3 flyer every saddled attack. 66% OH WR means it's a nightmare on curve behind a go-wide board. Saddle 4 needs support, but GW is the best archetype and this is a premier payoff; take it very early and build the wide team.
Slick Sequence: Efficient UR removal with upside — 2 damage for two mana, drawing a card when it's your second spell. That cantrip clause is easy to hit in a double-spell deck, making it a two-for-one. 55.6% GIH and a big +6.6 iwd; the removal-underrating effect applies. Solid early-mid pick and a reason to be in UR.
Taii Wakeen, Perfect Shot: Build-around RW rare that plays like a role-player. The card-draw trigger and X-damage boost want a burn/ping shell (pairs with Jolene, deserts, any noncombat damage), but at 53.1% WR and 45% play rate it's a fragile 2/3 that underdelivers without support. Good in a dedicated Boros direct-damage deck, mediocre otherwise.
Vial Smasher, Gleeful Grenadier: Good BR outlaws payoff, a solid mid-pick in the pair. A 3/2 for two that pings the opponent for each outlaw ETB — reach and reward in the aggressive shell. The +3.4 iwd and 69% play rate are strong, but the C+ grade and low toughness mean it needs the BR outlaw density to shine; filler elsewhere.
Vraska Joins Up: Trap rare — 43.2% GIH, negative IWD, and a 7.5% play rate expose it. Deathtouch counters on your board is a narrow combat upgrade and the legendary-damage draw rarely triggers, so it's a two-mana enchantment that doesn't affect the board enough. Skip it in normal GB.
Vraska, the Silencer: Excellent GB bomb — a 3-mana 3/3 deathtouch that trades into anything, and every opponent's nontoken creature that dies can be stolen back as a Treasure-ramp body. Top 2.3 ALSA and 78.8% play rate confirm first-pick pull in Golgari; deathtouch alone makes it always-good, the engine is upside.
Wrangler of the Damned: Underrated UW control engine that wheels to pick 6+ — a signal blue/UW is open. A 1/4 flash that pumps out 2/2 flyers each turn you don't cast from hand, grinding out any stalled board. 50.8% GIH undersells it in the right shell; LoL: 'if it's the last thing standing, that just wins.'
Wylie Duke, Atiin Hero: Excellent GW gold uncommon-power at rare — a 4/2 vigilance that draws a card and gains life every time it taps, so it advances your board AND blocks while refueling. 59.9% GIH and +5.4 IWD; the go-wide/tap synergies (saddle, convoke) make it even better. High pick in the best archetype.
Bandit's Haul: Fixing artifact that draws in crime decks — a role-player, not a card. Ramps any color and slowly loots via crime counters, so it smooths 4-5c/crime piles. 54.3% GIH is fine but the D grade warns it's low-impact; play it for fixing when you need it, not for the draw engine.
Boom Box: Filler/support. A colorless Nevinyrral's-lite that costs a backbreaking eight total mana to fire and only shines in the niche Eartha Joe doubling combo — 9.6% play rate and 51.8% GIH confirm it's rarely worth the slot. Playable colorless removal in a slow deck, but a low pick.
Gold Pan: Filler fixing, mostly sideboard/greedy-deck material. A 2-mana equipment that makes a Treasure and gives +1/+1 is slow, and 7.6 ALSA with 22.8% play says most decks pass it. Take it only when you need the fixing for a 4-5c splash pile; otherwise leave it.
Lavaspur Boots: Filler equipment. Cheap +1/+0, haste and ward can protect a threat, but it's low-impact and demands a good creature to matter; the -1.3 IWD, 11.6% play rate and C- grade mark it a fringe aggro inclusion. Usually a sideboard/last-slot card.
Luxurious Locomotive: Low-impact colorless Vehicle — a 6/5 for five, crew 1, that spews Treasures when it swings. 17% play rate, negative IWD, sub-50 GIH WR: it's too slow and clunky for a midrange format. A ramp/fixing curiosity for greedy multicolor piles at best; generally leave it in the sideboard.
Mobile Homestead: Sneaky-good colorless engine, strongest alongside Mounts (which grant it haste). A 3/3 crew-2 for two that filters lands into play on attack keeps your draws live and curves out. 56.3% GIH with a notably high 59.1% OH — plays great early. C grade undersells it; solid playable in any GW/Mounts or go-wide deck.
Oasis Gardener: The premier fixer for 4-5c/Desert good-stuff — Numot's foundational pick there. A {3} 2/2 that gains 2 and taps for any color is exactly the mana-and-lifegain a greedy crime/goodstuff pile wants; Kenji ran multiples. 54.4% WR is fine, but its real value is enabling the archetype. Priority in 5c, filler in a normal two-color deck.
Redrock Sentinel: Fringe colorless value/fixing, a niche playable. A 2/4 defender that sacs lands to draw and make Treasure — pure card advantage plus fixing for a 4-5c good-stuff pile. The 55% WR is soup-inflated by those decks; in a normal aggressive 40 the C- grade and defender body make it a sideboard-ish late pick.
Silver Deputy: Filler colorless common — a 1/2 that fetches a basic or Desert to the top and pumps a creature as a sorcery. Fixing plus a Desert tutor has a niche in 4-5c/Desert piles, but 50.5% GIH and negative IWD mark it as a weak body. Take late when you need fixing, otherwise pass.
Sterling Hound: Filler artifact body — a colorless 3/2 that surveils 2 on ETB, splashable in any deck but unexciting. 53.9% GIH with a 7.5 ALSA and 33.8% play rate mark it as a late-table replaceable; fine graveyard-fuel/curve-filler for BW/UB, but you're rarely happy maindecking it.
Tomb Trawler: Filler at best; the -2.9 IWD and 9.7% play rate say leave it out. A colorless 0/4 wall that only recurs graveyard hate — no clock, no card advantage. Playable as a defensive blocker in a slow deck starved for two-drops, but you'll cut it from most 40s.
Abraded Bluffs: Take the crime-desert freely — RW dual that enters tapped, pings an opponent for 1 (turning on Desert's Due and crime payoffs), and fixes for the weaker-color pair. 54.8% GIH is strong for a land; the ETB damage is real value. Good early-to-mid pick that keeps you open in RW/Naya.
Arid Archway: Trap — LoL's retro flags it explicitly. A colorless bounce-Desert that enters tapped and returns a land sets you back on tempo and produces no colored mana. 51.3% GIH and a -3.4 IWD confirm it hurts you; don't run this even in Desert decks.
Bristling Backwoods: Good fixing land, high pick in RG. A tapped RG dual that pings for one on ETB — dual-purpose fixing plus a crime trigger, and it turns on Desert's Due. 83% play rate; take it 2-4 in any red-green deck and don't pass a medium card for the last copy, but the tapland cost keeps it a support pick.
Conduit Pylons: Priority fixing land — take it early despite the D grade. It surveils on ETB and fixes any color, and 56.1% GIH on 91.9% play proves lands like this quietly win games by enabling your good cards and splashes. Grade misjudges fixing; this is a staple for multicolor and the crime/good-stuff piles.
Creosote Heath: High pick fixing — take it. A GW crime-desert that fixes, deals 1 (crime trigger) and turns on desert payoffs; only downside is entering tapped. The 56.1% GIH WR and 58.7% OH WR reflect its smoothing value. Grab 2-4 in GW/desert decks — keeps you open.
Eroded Canyon: Good UR crime-desert — enters tapped, pings an opponent for 1 (a free crime trigger), and fixes U/R. Solid 54.9% GIH WR with +3.0 IWD; take 2-4 for any UR deck, and higher if you have crime payoffs. Never pass a real card for it, but it's the ideal early-pack fixing that keeps you open.
Festering Gulch: Take the crime-desert early in BG or any crime/desert deck — it fixes GB mana, deals 1 to an opponent for a free crime trigger, and turns on Desert's Due. 56.6% GIH and 88% play. Dual-purpose land that keeps you open; never pass a medium card for one, but grab it over filler.
Forlorn Flats: Take it — dual-purpose WB desert that fixes and commits a crime. Enters tapped but pings an opponent (turning on Desert's Due and crime payoffs) while adding W or B; 56% WR and 83% play rate show the value. Grab 2-4 in any WB/BW crime deck; never pass a real card for it, but it's a strong land pick.
Jagged Barrens: Premium BR fixing and the archetype's signpost desert — take it highly in that pair. Enters tapped, pings the opponent for 1 (a free crime), taps for B or R. Turns on Desert's Due and crime payoffs while fixing. The 84% play rate and +2.5 iwd say it's a real pick; never pass it late in BR.
Lonely Arroyo: Take it — a WU crime-desert that fixes your mana, pings an opponent on ETB (a free crime trigger), and enters tapped. 54.9% GIH with +2.0 IWD is strong for a land. Premium for UW/UB crime and any deck wanting fixing; grab 2-4, but never over a real playable.
Lush Oasis: High-value GU fixing and crime enabler — enters tapped, pings an opponent (a free crime), and taps for G or U. 56.1% GIH and 82.1% play rate reflect that deserts are premium in this format; take it early for GU/4-5c good-stuff piles, it fixes and triggers crime payoffs.
Mirage Mesa: High pick — premium fixing that keeps you open and is itself a Desert. Enters tapped but taps for any color and turns on Desert's Due, Outcaster Greenblade and the rest. 95% play rate; both LoL ('really really strong') and Numot rate it above other duals. Take deserts and fixing early in this bomby, splash-heavy format.
Sandstorm Verge: Fringe utility desert — taps for colorless only, and the can't-block activation is a slow, expensive Falter. D grade and 43.9% play; the 54.7% GIH is just a land's baseline. Playable as a desert-count enabler in decks that want the subtype, but the colorless-only fixing is a real cost.
Soured Springs: High pick for UB — dual fixing plus a crime trigger. Taps for U/B and pings an opponent on ETB, so it fixes and enables Desert's Due/crime payoffs for free. 56.4% GIH and +4.1 IWD are excellent for a tapland; take these deserts early when you're in blue-black.
Jace Reawakened: Strong blue mythic that overperformed. The turn-4+ restriction is real, but +1 loot and +1 exile-and-plot generate steady advantage and the ultimate ends games — LoL's "Jace is real." 51.2% GIH looks soft because it's a slow-deck card; ALSA 2.2 and 75% play rate show it's a high pick for UB/UW control.
Bucolic Ranch: Narrow but fine fixing land for Mount decks. Colorless plus any-color-for-Mounts and a Mount-dig ability rewards a GW/RG Mount build; 56.1% GIH is solid but the 61% play rate reflects its restriction. Take it in a Mount-heavy deck, pass it otherwise — it's not general fixing.
