Blooming Marsh: Strong dual land for BG — high pick. Untapped early, fixes B/G cleanly, and quietly enables Honest Rutstein Abzan shells. Solid 53.7% GIH WR and 3.9 ALSA; premium fixing in a bomby format is always worth a real pick to keep your colors and splashes online.
Botanical Sanctum: Clean GU dual land — untapped early, fixes green/blue with no drawback beyond the turn-3 clause. Fixing is at a premium in a splash-happy format; the 53.8% GIH WR just reflects lands being lands. A high pick for any Simic or green/blue-based multicolor deck; grab it to enable your bombs and splashes.
Concealed Courtyard: Solid WB fixing that often enters untapped early. A painless dual that helps you splash or support BW crimes/recursion. The 54.4% GIH is inflated by fixing-hungry pilots, but fixing is genuinely valuable in this bomby format. Good pick when in WB/splashing; keeps you open. Mid-pick land.
Inspiring Vantage: Solid RW fixing — take it if you're in Boros or splashing. Fastland that untaps early keeps aggressive curves on track, and dual-color fixing is always at a premium here. 52.6% WR and 63% play rate; the negative IWD just reflects that lands don't win when drawn late. A clean, uncounted upgrade to your manabase.
Spirebluff Canal: Good UR fixing land, a fine pick for the pair. Untapped early, taps for U or R — clean dual fixing with no drawback in the opener. The 52.4% WR is unremarkable because lands don't win games when drawn late, but the fixing is worth a mid pick in any UR deck; prioritize over marginal spells.
Stoneforge Mystic: Bonus-sheet build-around, unplayable without Equipment — a tutor-and-cheat engine that's a blank 1/2 unless OTJ hands you a worthwhile Equipment to grab. Null OH/GD WR and 30.9% play rate reflect that it's often a sideboard. Provisional read: only maindeck it with real Equipment targets; otherwise pass.
Brazen Borrower: Premium blue mythic — a flash 3/1 flier that also bounces any nonland permanent (Vapor Snag with a body attached), giving huge tempo and flexibility. +8.4 iwd and 58.6% GIH with a 2.1 ALSA make it a slam first pick in any blue deck; among the best cards in your chunk.
Desertion: Bomb-tier control finisher: counter any spell, and if it's a creature or artifact you steal it onto your side — a two-for-one swing. 58% GIH, +8.0 IWD, A-grade. Premium in any UX control deck; snap it early. Only downside is needing UU up on turn five.
Morbid Opportunist: Strong black engine, mislabeled by its B- grade — a resilient 1/3 that draws a card whenever creatures die, and in a removal-heavy grindy format that's a card almost every turn. Elite 1.8 ALSA and +5.2 IWD; premier card advantage for UB/BW/GB midrange. Take it early.
Port Razer: Overrated mythic — a trap in most decks. A 4/4 for five with no evasion needing to connect for extra combats is fragile and slow; null OH/GD data and a 48.6% GIH with negative IWD show it underperforms. Only shines in a fast, wide RG board — otherwise a mediocre body.
Scapeshift: Unplayable in Limited. Sacrificing lands to fetch the same number back is card-neutral do-nothing with no basics to ramp into — the F grade and 1.9% play rate say it all. Null WR because nobody runs it; leave it in the pack. Provisional, but the read is clear.
Mystic Snake: Strong UG tempo bomb-answer. Flash 2/2 that hard-counters a spell is a clean two-for-one against the format's many bombs, and exile-adjacent disruption is at a premium here. 55.6% GIH understates it — the 1GUU cost and reactive nature deflate the raw rate; +5.4 IWD is the truer read. High pick when you're base-blue.
Notion Thief: Trap in Limited. A 3/1 flash body whose draw-steal ability rarely does much in a normal game, and the awful 41.6% OH WR / 46.8% GIH WR expose it — it's a constructed card. The C grade is generous; only a fine surprise blocker, essentially unplayable maindeck.
Desert: Fine colorless Desert utility land — taps for {C} and can ping an attacker for 1 at end of combat, plus it turns on Desert's Due, Outcaster Greenblade, etc. The colorless mana is a real cost in a two-color deck, but the Desert-matters synergies and free removal make it a strong pick for green/black desert builds.
Prismatic Vista: Fetchland — Big Score fixing that thins and enables any splash for a point of life. 97% play because it always makes your deck, but the 53.0% GIH and -0.9 iwd show it doesn't win games by itself; it's a smoothing tool, not power. Take it when you want fixing for a greedy build, otherwise a low priority.
Collector's Cage: Bomb — first-pick mythic. {1}{W} that hides away a card and, in a go-wide board with varied powers, repeatedly grows a creature AND casts the hidden card for free. Trivial to enable in GW/RW. 62.4% GIH WR, +8.2 IWD, 1.8 ALSA, 94% play rate — elite in the format's best decks. Take it over nearly everything.
Grand Abolisher: Narrow constructed reprint that's mediocre in Limited — a 2/2 for WW whose lockout ability rarely matters in a fair 40. The 50.9% GIH WR and negative iwd confirm it plays as a vanilla two-drop despite the mythic tag. A filler body for aggressive white; don't value the text.
Oltec Matterweaver: Premium white mythic, a near-bomb — 57.2% GIH, +3.0 IWD, 91.7% play rate off a 1.8 ALSA. A 2/4 for three that makes a Gnome (or copies an artifact token) every creature cast is a snowballing go-wide engine that also blocks well. Slam it; it powers GW/token boards. First-pickable.
Rest in Peace: Trap/sideboard — total graveyard hate that does nothing to the board and actively hurts your own recursion in a format full of it. Null WR with a 0.5% play rate and F grade confirm it's unplayable in a normal 40; leave it in the sideboard against Honest Rutstein/reanimator decks.
Esoteric Duplicator: Unplayable outside a dedicated artifact deck that doesn't exist here — F grade, 44.7% GIH, 7.7% play rate. It's a Clue that copies artifacts you sacrifice, a build-around with no support in OTJ Limited. Read is provisional on tiny data but the direction is clear: don't play it.
Simulacrum Synthesizer: Build-around mythic with almost no support here — needs a critical mass of MV3+ artifacts to make Constructs, which OTJ Limited rarely provides. Only 8.0% play rate and null OH/GD data; the +8.7 IWD is from the handful of dedicated artifact decks. Read is provisional but this is a near-unplayable niche, skip it.
Worldwalker Helm: Effectively unplayable in Limited. It only does anything with a critical mass of artifact tokens to copy, and the 3.5% play rate with null WR confirms nobody found a home. Provisional read, but the D grade is right — leave it in the sideboard unless you're deep in a token build.
Greed's Gambit: Trap mythic. The ETB is explosive — three cards, six life, three fliers — but the brutal end-step tax (discard, lose 2, sac a creature) bleeds you out and the leave-the-battlefield clause is a disaster. 50.7% GIH, -0.5 IWD, 17% play rate; C- is right, a low pick you usually cut.
Harvester of Misery: Elite bomb — near a first pick. A 5/4 menace that wipes the opponent's board with -2/-2 on ETB, and if that's not needed it's a removal spell you discard (1B, -2/-2). 61.3% GIH, +9.3 IWD, 1.7 ALSA: it's the whole package. Slam it in any black deck.
Hostile Investigator: Bomb mythic — first-pick. A 4/3 that strips a card on ETB and investigates off any discard, generating card advantage in most black decks. Elite 63.1% GIH WR, +10.0 IWD, 1.6 ALSA — the B+ grade undersells a top-tier value engine. Slam it.
Generous Plunderer: Strong red mythic and an aggressive Treasure engine — a menacing 2/2 that ramps you a Treasure each upkeep and punches the opponent for their artifact count. 62.8% OH WR shows it's a proactive threat that snowballs; the 'gift' Treasure feeds its own attack trigger. High pick in any red aggro or Treasure-leaning deck.
Legion Extruder: Underrated Big Score/artifact bomb — take it high in any red or artifact deck. ETB 2 damage to any target is removal on a permanent that then grinds out 3/3 Golems by sacrificing artifacts. B+ grade and 55.1% GIH; the removal-plus-engine package is exactly what a grindy format wants. Early pick, best in RG/artifact shells.
Memory Vessel: Unplayable — the F grade and 1.1% play rate are correct. It exiles both players' top seven and locks you out of your hand, a symmetric five-mana do-nothing with no board impact in a midrange format. Provisional on stats (null WR) but the read isn't close. Never maindeck.
Molten Duplication: Trap; the D grade and 45.4% WR are damning. 1R to copy a creature/artifact with haste that you sacrifice at end of turn is a tempo/combo card with no lasting board — the 11.1% play rate says almost no one wants it. Effectively unplayable in a normal deck; leave it.
Territory Forge: Trap mythic, effectively unplayable — F grade, null WR, 1.7% play rate. A five-mana artifact that steals another artifact/land's activated abilities does nothing on an empty-ish board and answers no threat. Provisional but clear: never maindeck it. Leave it in the pack.
Ancient Cornucopia: Mediocre fixing artifact for 4-5c piles — taps for any color and drips small lifegain on colored spells, but it's slow and does nothing to the board. 50.9% GIH and negative iwd undercut the mythic grade; play it only as a mana rock in greedy multicolor decks, otherwise pass.
Bristlebud Farmer: Bomb — first-pick green. A 5/5 trample for four that makes two Food (lifegain/fixing fodder) and turns attacks into card-advantage digs. A-grade, 63% opening-hand WR, +8.9 IWD, 94% play rate. Overloaded rate, resilience and value in one card; take it over almost anything.
Omenpath Journey: Below-rate green ramp/fixing enchantment — spends turn four to slowly trickle lands in one per end step, too slow and low-impact for a bombs-and-removal format. C- grade, flat +0.7 IWD, and 27.1% play rate all agree. Only for a greedy 4-5c fixing pile that needs the lands; otherwise pass.
Sandstorm Salvager: Bomb — a top-tier green mythic. Three-mana for four power across two bodies with an anthem/trample activation that snowballs tokens is elite in any go-wide green deck. 60.9% GIH, +6.4 IWD, and a 1.5 ALSA make it a clear early pick; grade B+ undersells it.
Vaultborn Tyrant: Format-defining bomb, first-pick. A 6/6 trample that draws and gains life off every big creature and copies itself on death — nearly impossible to deal with 2-for-1. 64.2% GIH, +10.6 IWD, A+, 95% play rate: take it over almost everything and let it anchor your green deck.
Loot, the Key to Everything: Build-around trap for most drafters. 53.8% GIH with a huge OH/GD gap (50.0 vs 56.0) and 28.1% play means it does nothing without a diverse permanent-type board to fuel it — a 1/2 that dies to a stiff breeze first. Only a dedicated Temur/artifacts-enchantments pile wants it; provisional pass.
Pest Control: Sideboard/niche only. A WB one-sided sweeper of 1-MV permanents with cycling as a floor, but it's dead against most boards; the null GIH WR, 2.7% play rate and D+ grade confirm a fringe card. Provisional read: cycle it away unless facing a token/aggro deck.
Lost Jitte: Powerful colorless equipment mythic — {1} to cast, {1} to equip, and every combat hit banks a counter for +1/+1, unblockable-enabling, or ramp. ALSA 1.8 and 91% play rate confirm it's a first-pickable colorless payoff that snowballs any aggressive board. Take it early; goes in every deck and closes games.
Lotus Ring: The D grade is a badly outdated theory read — the live 56.3% GIH and 80% play tell the real story. Indestructible +3/+3 and vigilance is a hard-to-answer threat that also cashes out for three mana of any color if the creature's in danger. Solid playable in any deck; trust the WR over the grade. Mid pick.
Nexus of Becoming: Bomb-tier colorless mythic — take it in any deck. Six mana, but every combat it draws AND can copy your best artifact/creature as a 3/3 Golem, snowballing card and board advantage no removal-light deck can race. 58.1% WR, +4.5 IWD, 2.0 ALSA, 94% play. Goes in every archetype; a top-end payoff that ends grindy games.
Sword of Wealth and Power: Bomb-tier colorless equipment and a slam first pick — 93.9% play rate, ALSA 1.6. +2/+2, protection from instants/sorceries (dodges most removal), Treasures on damage, and copies your next spell. Goes in any deck, warps combat, hard to answer. The 52.6% WR undersells it because it's an every-deck staple; take it P1.
Torpor Orb: Narrow hate-piece bonus-sheet card, unplayable in a normal 40 — 0.6% play rate, F grade. Shutting off ETB triggers hoses this ETB-heavy format but also blanks half your own deck. Provisional: sideboard curio at best, do not maindeck. Take only as a late speculative hate card.
Transmutation Font: Slow build-around, mostly a trap in a normal 40 — a 5-mana rock that makes tokens and can tutor an artifact after grinding three different ones. 50.0% GIH with OH just 46.7% shows it's a do-nothing when drawn early; leave it for dedicated artifact decks, filler at best elsewhere.
Fomori Vault: Fringe/filler land — a colorless source with an artifact-count card-selection ability that does little without an artifact deck OTJ doesn't support. 50% GIH is exactly break-even and the 7.9% play rate says pass. Provisional read on thin data, but this is a build-around miss for normal decks.
Tarnation Vista: Fine fixing land — enters tapped for one chosen color, with a filter mode that can produce multiple colors of mana in a multicolor board. 90.5% play rate shows it goes in any greedy deck, but the flat 0.0 IWD and enters-tapped cost mean it's a fixing role-player, not a power pick. Grab for 3+ color piles.
Fell the Mighty: Premium white sweeper, a high pick in control/go-wide. Cast targeting your own small creature to wipe the opponent's bigger board — asymmetric against green fatties and bombs. 55.7% GIH underrates it (sweepers win by being held); the A- grade and 3.0 ALSA are the truer read.
Fierce Retribution: Solid white removal, high pick. Two-mana destroy-an-attacker is efficient defensive removal, and the Cleave option to hit any creature for 5W adds flexibility late. GIH underrates removal, so value it above its 54.7%; a strong pick in any white deck, though it's reactive so don't take it over a bomb.
Journey to Nowhere: Premium white removal — high pick. Two-mana exile-a-creature (until this enchantment leaves) is exactly the clean answer this bomby format demands, and exile beats destroy given all the recursion. 58.4% GIH on 93% play, 2.6 ALSA: take it early in any white deck.
Leyline Binding: Premium exile removal — high pick, and exile is at a premium here. Flash exiling any nonland permanent, cheap in a multicolor/desert manabase; even at full cost it answers bombs. Strong 56.9% GIH WR and 2.8 ALSA; the B- grade undersells efficient exile in this recursion-heavy format.
Pariah: Trap rare — an Aura that redirects all your damage to one creature, a fragile combo-ish 'fog' that dies to any removal and does nothing to the board. 19% play rate, sub-50 GIH WR, negative IWD: it's a build-around that doesn't come together in Limited. Leave it in the sideboard.
Path to Exile: Premium removal and a Big Score gem — exile is extra-valuable here given how much recursion the format has. One mana to answer any creature, including bombs, at the cost of a land you can play around late. 56.6% GIH, ALSA 2.3, 90% play. Grab it near the top of the pack in any white deck.
Archive Trap: Unplayable in a normal 40 despite tempting numbers. Mill-13 does nothing to the board, and the free-cast clause requires the opponent to search their library — which almost never happens in this format. The 57.9% GIH WR and +9.3 IWD are a tiny self-selected mill sample; F grade is right. Only in a dedicated mill combo.
Archmage's Charm: Powerful but color-intensive rare; the UUU cost caps it. Counter, draw two, or steal a small permanent — flexible and strong, but only heavy-blue decks cast it (33% play rate reflects that). The +5.7 iwd and 57% drawn WR show the ceiling when you can pay it; a high pick if you're base-blue, otherwise a hate-pick.
Commandeer: Near-unplayable rare — 45.8% GIH, D- grade, 5.9% play rate. Seven mana (or a steep two-blue-card pitch) to steal a noncreature spell is far too situational in a creature-dense Limited format where most decks lean on bodies. Leave it; it rarely has a live target when you need it.
Essence Capture: Solid blue tempo counter — hard-counters a creature spell for UU and puts a +1/+1 counter on your board. +5.6 iwd and 55.7% GIH make it a reliable playable in UB/UW control/tempo; the double-pip and creature-only clause cap it below premium removal, but it answers bombs on the stack.
Mana Drain: Bomb — one of the best Big Score reprints. Hard counter that ramps you the countered spell's mana value, effectively a Time Walk into your bomb. 59.7% GIH, +9.8 IWD, A-. Take it near the top in any blue seat; UU on two is trivial to hold up.
Mindbreak Trap: Sideboard-only trap, unplayable maindeck — its free mode needs the opponent to cast three spells in a turn, which never happens in Limited, so it's a clunky 2UU hard counter otherwise. Null WR, 5% play, D- grade. Do not maindeck.
Repulse: Solid blue tempo card, plays anywhere. Bounce plus a card replaces itself, so it's never dead — remove a blocker, save a creature, reset an aura. 57.5% GIH and +6.2 IWD with 86% play rate make it a reliable role-player; a fine pick that smooths any blue deck.
Heartless Pillage: Niche BR uncommon. Two-card discard plus a raid Treasure is disruption-plus-ramp, but hand attack is weak in a creature-driven midrange format — the 49% play rate and C- grade reflect that. The +2.9 IWD is aggro-conditional; a low pick that's fine as BR curve filler, not a priority.
Imp's Mischief: Niche/sideboard trick, not a maindeck card. Redirecting a spell for 1B plus life is a blowout in narrow spots but blank most of the time — 47.1% GIH, 43.6% OH, 25.5% play confirm it's too situational. Leave it in the board and bring it in against removal-heavy or targeted-spell decks.
Murder: Premium black removal — high pick. Unconditional instant-speed creature kill, exactly the point-and-click answer this bomby format rewards. The 56.6% GIH WR and +4.5 IWD understate it since GIH underrates removal; the double-black cost is the only knock. Take it early.
Overwhelming Forces: Game-ending black mythic bomb — a one-sided wrath that also refills your hand by the number destroyed. Eight mana is steep but 65% GIH WR and +13.3 IWD mean it wins nearly every game it resolves in this grindy format. First-pick-caliber; the reason to be base-black and go long.
Reanimate: High-value Big Score card, best in graveyard/recursion decks (BG/BW) but playable anywhere as one-mana cheat-a-bomb. Reanimating an opponent's dead bomb or your own for a life payment is a huge tempo/mana swing. 53.8% GIH; the life loss and empty-yard games keep it from being a slam. Solid speculative pick in black.
Surgical Extraction: Not a Limited card — F grade, 1.1% play rate. One-mana (or 2 life) graveyard hate that names a single card is a narrow sideboard tool with no board impact. Provisional on null WR, but recursion-heavy though the format is, this is far too surgical to maindeck. Leave it in the box.
Thoughtseize: Strong disruption reprint, a mid-to-high pick. One mana to strip their bomb or removal, losing 2 life — excellent proactive answer in a format decided by individual card power, especially in slower UB/BW. The +4.0 iwd and 74.6% play rate beat the cautious C grade; trust the live number and take it.
Collective Defiance: Premium flexible red rare, an early pick — 55.4% GIH and B+ grade with a fine 81.7% play rate. Escalate lets it be 4 to a creature, 3 to the face, and/or a wheel, so it's removal that never rots in hand. Take it high in any red deck (BR/RW/UR); the modality is the value.
Crackle with Power: Bomb finisher — a scalable X-spell that deals five-times-X to multiple targets, a two-plus-for-one removal blowout or a face-burn kill. 58.8% GIH with GD 61.8% and A- grade confirm it wins games; a high pick in any red deck, though it wants the late game to shine.
Electrodominance: Strong flexible removal/finisher for red decks: instant-speed X damage to anything, plus a free spell of MV X or less as a bonus. The 53% GIH undersells scalable removal; the +1.4 IWD and 77% play rate are the real read. Kills bombs late, snipes creatures early. High pick in any red deck.
Fling: Niche finisher, not a maindeck card — sacrificing a creature for reach damage is card disadvantage and only shines as a surprise kill with a fattie or sac-payoff. C-, 50.8% GIH, 19.3% play rate. Sideboard tech for an aggressive RG/BR deck; leave it out otherwise.
Indomitable Creativity: Unplayable in Limited. A triple-red XRRR sorcery that destroys and randomly reanimates has no reliable payoff in a 40, and the 2.1% play rate with null WR says so. Provisional but clear — the D grade holds; never maindeck this.
Skewer the Critics: Solid red burn, take it. 2R for 3 to any target, castable for a single R with spectacle in an aggressive deck — flexible reach and creature removal. B grade and 53.4% GIH (removal is underrated by GIH); a reliable early-to-mid pick in BR/RW aggro, less exciting in a slow deck.
Skullcrack: Trap — don't maindeck it. Burn to the face only (can't hit creatures) is far too narrow in a grindy midrange format: 45.6% GIH, 13% play. It's a sideboard reach card for a fully-built BR/RW burn deck at best, and even then marginal. Pass.
Clear Shot: Premium green removal — high pick. A fight spell that pumps your creature +1/+1 and forces near-guaranteed one-sided kills at instant speed, one of green's best answers. 57.5% GIH WR, +2.9 IWD and 2.8 ALSA; GIH underrates it, so value it above the B- grade in GW/GB.
Force of Vigor: Sideboard-only green mythic — free (pitch a green card) double artifact/enchantment destruction, but there aren't enough targets maindeck. Null live WR with just 6% play rate and a D grade; provisionally a dead card in game 1, a strong bring-in against artifact/aura-heavy decks. Don't maindeck it.
Pest Infestation: Excellent scalable green bomb — 61.1% GIH, +7.4 iwd, ALSA 2.4. Even a small X floods the board with Pests (chumps, saddle fodder, lifegain) while blowing up artifacts/enchantments as needed; late-game it's a game-ending army. B grade undersells it. High pick in any green deck, especially GW/RG go-wide.
Primal Command: Overrated ceiling, plays like a role-player — the C- grade is closer than the 57.5% WR. At {3}{G}{G} the modal package (gain 7, bounce a noncreature permanent, tutor a creature, graveyard shuffle) is flexible value but slow and boardless. 82% play rate is soup/goodstuff inflation. Fine top-end for a grindy green deck, not a slam.
Primal Might: Premium green removal masquerading as a pump spell — a high pick, ALSA 2.2, 92.7% play rate. XG pumps your creature then fights, killing almost anything while growing your board; scales all game. The +3.9 iwd and 58.1% WR are real, and GIH WR underrates fight removal. Prioritize in any green deck.
Thornado: Situational green removal — kills a flyer or cycles when there's no target, so it's never fully dead. But green struggles for interaction and a flyers-only Naturalize is narrow; 50.2% GIH and negative IWD with 27% play rate mark it as a sideboard-leaning role-player. Playable filler, not a priority.
Abrupt Decay: Premium two-color removal — uncounterable, destroys any nonland permanent MV 3 or less at instant speed, answering most of the format's problem cards for two mana. 57.1% GIH understates it since GIH underrates removal; a top pick that pushes you into GB/Golgari, always maindeck.
Anguished Unmaking: Premium catch-all removal — exile any nonland permanent at instant speed, answering bombs, enchantments and recursion targets (exile is at a premium here). The 54% GIH underrates it as removal typically does; the 3-life cost is real in aggro mirrors but trivial in WB/BW midrange. Take it high.
Back for More: Strong BG uncommon — a reanimation-plus-fight that returns your best dead creature AND kills one of theirs, a two-for-one that punishes the format's recursion-heavy grind. 56.9% GIH and B+ grade; six mana is the only knock. Honest Rutstein GB value decks love it. Good mid pick.
Bedevil: Premium removal — destroy anything relevant at instant speed. Kills artifacts, creatures, and planeswalkers, exactly what a bomby format wants, though BBR is a real color commitment. 53.0% GIH slightly underrates it as removal often does; prioritize it highly when you're base-black in BR.
Buried in the Garden: Premium GW removal, high pick. Exile any nonland permanent — hits bombs and enchantments, and exile matters against this recursion-heavy format — while ramping and fixing your mana. 59.6% GIH, +4.9 IWD, 88% play rate; a strong early pick that Buried is one of the best answers white-green gets.
Crime // Punishment: Flexible WBG value card, middling but playable. The Crime half steals a creature/enchantment from a graveyard (great vs recursion) and Punishment is an X-cost sweeper — real utility, but 3WB//XBG is demanding and 54.7% GIH is unremarkable. A fine pickup for a WB/GB grind deck with the fixing, not a slam.
Cruel Ultimatum: Build-around top-end, not a slam. A crushing UBR seven-drop that wins if you can cast it, but the {U}{U}{B}{B}{B}{R}{R} cost demands a fixing-rich pile; the inflated 61.4% GIH WR / +13.0 IWD is the successful-caster's number. C- grade reflects the cost. Only in a 4-5c good-stuff deck.
Decimate: Trap-flagged RG rare — the four-target requirement (artifact AND creature AND enchantment AND land) makes it frequently uncastable; the 43% GIH WR and -6.7 IWD reflect that it bricks in hand. Grades tempt you (C+) but the live data is damning. A situational blowout you can rarely rely on; low priority even in RG.
Decisive Denial: Flexible GU role-player — a fight spell that doubles as a soft counter. The fight mode is real removal in a green creature deck; the Force Spike mode is situational insurance. 53.7% GIH and 41% play mark it as a good-not-great playable that needs GU. Mid pick when the pair is open; the fight half carries it.
Detention Sphere: Solid UW removal — take it fairly early in a control shell. {1}{W}{U} exiles any nonland permanent (and copies of it), answering bombs and go-wide tokens, though it's temporary if the Sphere dies. 55% WR, +4.7 IWD, 64% play. Two-color cost restricts it to UW, where it's a premium flexible answer.
Endless Detour: Powerful but three-color-locked answer — 14.9% play rate shows how rarely you can cast GWU. Flexible tempo/removal that bounces a spell, permanent, or graveyard card to top or bottom of library (soft-exile vs recursion). The 55.8% WR is the number when it's castable; only for a Bant/4-5c fixing pile, a hate-pick otherwise.
Fractured Identity: Bomb mythic and premium exile removal in one — 63.1% GIH with a massive +12.1 IWD, best card in this chunk. Exiling the opponent's best threat (dodging the format's rampant recursion) AND copying it is a two-card swing. UW gold, splashable. First-pick, slam it every time.
Hindering Light: Narrow protective counter — stops a spell targeting you or your stuff and cantrips, but it's dead when the opponent isn't targeting you. 49.1% GIH, 45.9% OH, and a 14% play rate confirm it's a sideboard card at best in UW; don't maindeck it.
Humiliate: Above-average WB disruption, better than its 37% play rate suggests: proactive Thoughtseize that also grows a creature, so it's never fully dead. +4.6 IWD and 57.8% GIH. Strips their bomb or removal before it lands — great in grindy BW/UB, a solid role-player elsewhere.
Hypothesizzle: Solid UR two-for-one — draw two and, if you have a spare nonland, deal 4 to a creature, so it's card advantage that doubles as removal. 53.4% GIH is a touch soft because five mana at instant speed is clunky, but the flexibility is real. Good playable for UR late-game control.
Ionize: Situational counter, only for UR control. Counter plus 2 damage is strong on the draw but dead when you're behind or tapped out, and the 37.6% play rate shows most decks can't support it. 55.0% GIH with a huge OH/GD split (50.4 vs 57.7) flags it as a reactive, deck-dependent card.
Oko, Thief of Crowns: Absolute bomb, P1P1 over nearly anything. +1 neuters any bomb or removes any attacker by Elk-ing it to a 3/3, +2 grinds Food, and he protects himself endlessly. 64.2% GIH, +13.3 IWD, ALSA 1.3, A+: the best card in most packs. Take it and figure out colors later.
Outlaws' Merriment: Bomb enchantment — high pick in RW/white go-wide. A free hasty creature every upkeep with lifelink/burn/trample upside snowballs and grinds through removal; 57.9% GIH, +5.4 IWD, 2.8 ALSA, A-grade all agree. Slam it in any Boros or white aggro shell.
Ride Down: Situational aggro removal for RW. Kills a blocker AND grants trample to punch through, a real blowout in go-wide Boros combat, but it does nothing on defense or an empty board; the 53.2% GIH WR and negative IWD peg it a conditional RW aggro playable.
Savage Smash: Decent RG removal — a fight spell with +2/+2, so your creature survives the trade and kills up. Fighting is worse than one-sided removal (needs a body, risks a blowout), hence the -1.4 IWD, but GIH WR underrates efficient removal per doctrine. A solid role-player in RG/green stompy where you have big creatures to swing it.
Siphon Insight: Strong UB card advantage with reach — a two-mana instant that steals two cards' worth of value (one now, one on flashback). 55.9% GIH and a healthy +5.3 iwd back the grind plan. C grade is too low. Solid mid pick that rewards the UB control shell; the color-fixed casting on the stolen card is a bonus.
Terminal Agony: Clean BR removal with upside — high pick in Rakdos. {2}{B}{R} unconditionally destroys any creature, and Madness lets you cast it for {B}{R} off a discard outlet for tempo and card filtering. 53.5% WR undersells it (removal underrating); the format needs answers to bombs. Efficient, gold-cost keeps it in BR — prioritize it there.
Tyrant's Scorn: Premium UB removal and a high pick for the pair. UB to hard-kill a creature MV 3 or less or bounce anything at instant speed — cheap, flexible, and always live. The +7.2 iwd and 59.5% drawn WR are excellent, and GIH WR still underrates cheap removal. Grab it early in any UB deck.
Vanishing Verse: Premium removal — two-mana exile any monocolored permanent, hitting nearly everything in a set full of mono threats and dodging recursion. 58.9% GIH with +5.7 IWD, and GIH famously underrates clean removal, so it's even better than it reads. High pick that pulls you into WB/BW; slam when in those colors.
Villainous Wealth: High-ceiling Sultai finisher — an X-spell that exiles and free-casts the opponent's top X, a game-ending value blowout in the 4-5c good-stuff/crime pile. A- grade and GD 57.8% look great, but OH 48.0% and soup inflation warn it's the built-around deck's number; prioritize only when you're the ramp/fixing pile.
Void Rend: Premium removal gated behind a WUB manabase — uncounterable destroy any nonland permanent at instant speed. The low 26% play rate is a fixing constraint, not a power one; the +6.3 IWD and 58% drawn WR show it slaps when cast. High pick if you're already three colors or have the fixing to splash.
Voidslime: Narrow rare with a heavy triple-pip Simic cost — a flexible counter (spell/activated/triggered) that's a blowout when it lands but demands you hold up GUU and play reactively, awkward in a proactive format. The stark 44.8% OH vs 56.6% GD split and 16.5% play rate show it punishes you when clogging your hand. Playable in dedicated GU control only.
Contagion Engine: Sideboard card, not a maindeck bomb here. Six mana for a one-sided -1/-1 sweep is too slow, and Numot pegs it as a fine board-in only against Outlaws' small creatures. 53.3% GIH is inflated by late-game grinds; the low oh_wr (49.2%) shows it does nothing early — mostly a trap.
Grindstone: Build-around trap for a normal deck. A one-mana mill artifact that's an unreliable win-con only in dedicated UB control ("a free win-con that commits crimes") — but the 42.6% GIH, -6.2 IWD and 36% OH WR show it's dead weight in a random 40. Speculative late pick for a crime/mill UB pile only; F otherwise.
Mindslaver: Overpriced novelty, roughly replacement-level. 51.0% GIH and +0.3 IWD say the 6-mana artifact plus 4-to-activate rarely swings a Limited game meaningfully — you spend ten mana to take one turn. Playable as colorless top-end filler in a slow control deck, but never a priority pick.
Unlicensed Hearse: Strong UB crime enabler + graveyard hate — high pick in that pair. Commits a free crime every turn while growing into a threat and exiling recursion targets, which matters given how much this format recurs. LoL rates it highly for UB crimes; 53.1% GIH WR undersells its engine role.
Dust Bowl: Unplayable in Limited — a colorless land whose only ability is grinding down nonbasics for 3+sac each activation, far too slow and card-negative. F grade, 5% play rate, 47% GIH WR all agree. Never maindeck; it's a Constructed toy that does nothing to win a 40-card game.
